\\\"reading_scope\\\": \\\"excerpt\\\", \\\"category\\\": \\\"related_chapter\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"[EXCERPT extracted-character range 0:3083]\\\\n# K-ALG-014：多 LoRA 服务：低秩计算、驻留与缓存身份\\\\n\\\\nLoRA 将任务适配表示为共享基座上的低秩增量。多 adapter 服务同时面对三个问题：如何共享基座矩阵乘而保留每行的增量；如何让 adapter、KV 和执行缓冲共同满足容量；如何保证请求、缓存和在途读取使用同一版本。支持加载很多 adapter 文件，并不等于能同时执行这些 adapter。\\\\n\\\\n## 数学对象与执行边界\\\\n\\\\n采用列向量约定。一个目标线性层的基座为 W₀∈R^{dₒ×dᵢ}，输入 x∈R^{dᵢ}，adapter 给出 A∈R^{r×dᵢ}、B∈R^{dₒ×r} 和缩放 s：\\\\n\\\\nΔW=sBA，u=Ax，y=W₀x+sBu。\\\\n\\\\nr 是因子内维，rank(BA)≤min(r,dᵢ,dₒ)，不应把因子内维和增量矩阵的实际秩混为一谈。低秩服务通常选择 r≪min(dᵢ,dₒ)；可支持的 r、dtype 和布局还受执行器限制。r=0 在本章表示无增量的基座路径，直接跳过分支；若配置用 s=α/r 表示缩放，必须在 r=0 前分支，不能计算除零。\\\\n\\\\nLoRA 原论文 §4.1 使用 W₀x+BAx，与本章约定一致。S-LoRA 使用行向量 xᵣWᵣ+xᵣAᵣBᵣ，其中 Aᵣ 为 dᵢ×r、Bᵣ 为 r×dₒ；转成列向量时 W₀=Wᵣᵀ、A=Aᵣᵀ、B=Bᵣᵀ。不能直接把行向量图中的矩阵形状搬进列向量算例。\\\\n\\\\n一个 adapter 是完整的不可变对象：基座兼容身份、对象版本、目标矩阵集合、每个矩阵的 A/B、有效 r、scale、数值表示和布局。一次请求绑定该对象，后续路由别名更新不改变已有绑定。设备驻留还需要物理页、页代次、加载完成关系、请求/图引用和实际读者；主机中有对象，不代表设备内容已经可读。\\\\n\\\\n共享计算发生在每个目标线性层内部。该层可将不同 adapter 请求的当前输入列组成 X，统一计算 W₀X，再按行归属加各自增量。上一层的增量已经改变隐藏状态，下一层必须使用更新后的输入。不能先独立执行完整基座模型，再在末尾加一个由原始输入算出的 adapter 修正。\\\\n\\\\n输入包括请求生命期、基座与 adapter 版本、当前层输入、token 逻辑位置、行映射、状态句柄和本轮容量。输出是原请求顺序的层结果，以及模型继续执行后产生的状态和完成责任。LoRA 线性分支本身不完成 Attention、KV 管理或采样。\\\\n\\\\n## 合法条件与方案选择\\\\n\\\\n固定 adapter 可计算 W′=W₀+sBA，以普通线性层执行。合并需要更新完整、没有读者正在使用被覆盖的存储，并满足声明的数值契约。保留多个合并副本会复制完整基座；只保留一个副本并串行切换则放弃跨 adapter 聚批机会。两种方案都可能合法，选择由切换频率、容量和负载决定。\\\\n\\\\n实数恒等式不保证浮点逐位一致。合并改变乘加顺序；量化基座还可能经历反量化、相加和重量化。运行时分支也有输入转换、低秩累加、scale 应用和最终相加的精度选择。比较时应固定参考表示、误差容限和输出判据。若 logits 的最大值与次大值间隔为 m，而每个 logit 的绝对误差不超过 ε，则 m>2ε 是保持该次 argmax 的充分条件；这不保证后续随机采样或整段文本完全一致。\\\\n\\\\n按 adapter 分组必须保留输入行到输出行的逆映射。相同 r 只说明形状相容，不说明 A/B、scale 或版本相同。分组键至少能唯一确定该层使用的完整 adapter 对象；未被该 adapter 作用的层走零增量路径。\\\\n\\\\n补齐到 R≥r 的一种充分构造是 A′=[A;0]、B′=[B,0]，于是 B′A′=BA。scale 保持原来的 s；若原来 s=α/r，不能因为物理桶宽改成 R 就改为 α/R。两侧补零是便于审计的规则，代数上更一般的条件是新增部分乘积为零。实际实现仍应初始化全部可能读取的 padding，不能依靠未初始化值碰巧抵消。该推导假设有限输入和可接受的中间数值；含 Inf/NaN 时，0×Inf 并不产生零，须拒绝、显式屏蔽或另订数值契约。\\\\n\\\\n缓存身份由状态生成的依赖闭包决定。相同 token 在不同 adapter 下可能产生不同 K/V，即使 adapter 没有直接修改某层的 K/V 投影，上游隐藏状态也可能已经改变。默认将影响状态的 adapter 身份及版本纳入 key；只有证明某类状态不依赖该 adapter，才可省略。例如仅作用于最终输出头的增量不必影响此前已生成的 KV。\\\\n\\\\n可以用完整身份 η 描述基座版本、adapter 对象版本、位置规则、数值表示、分片布局和模态条件，再以父前缀身份、本块 token、块边界及隔离命名空间组织缓存。哈希负责检索，碰撞处理和精确身份核对仍需有契约。salt 不替代授权。固定 vLLM 文档明确把 LoRA ID 列入额外哈希并仅缓存完整块；若允许同一 ID 更新权重，还要增加版本或内容身份。已有 KV 不要求 adapter 权重始终驻留，但后续执行该 adapter 时必须恢复相同对象。\\\\n\\\\n## 每层计算、加载与完成的完整路径\\\\n\\\\n下面选择一种保守组织：一轮执行前预留整批所需 adapter、KV 增量和缓冲；该轮使用不可变描述；资源不足则减少批次、等待或拒绝。逐层换入或分波执行也是候选，但需要重新推导传输、容量和完成关系。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\n输入：请求快照；每层基座；不可变 adapter 仓库；设备页池；状态与输出预算\\\\n输出：按请求归属的结果；已完成的新状态；加载、引用和回收责任\\\\n\\\\n初始化空计划、临时预留集合和行表 I\\\\n在协调区内，对候选请求逐一处理：\\\\n    校验基座兼容、完整 A/B 形状、scale、目标层、数值与分片契约\\\\n    固定对象身份 (adapter_id, version)，建立行到请求/位置的映射\\\\n    计算尚未驻留的唯一对象、KV 增量和执行缓冲的物理需求\\\\n    模拟合法淘汰；只使用已经满足回收条件的容量\\\\n    若加入后不可行，跳过或调整该候选，不发布不完整计划\\\\n    取得已有对象保护，预留新对象目的页及必要 staging\\\\n    任一步失败，撤销该候选已取得的临时资源，保留原请求状态\\\\n\\\\n对新对象执行加载：\\\\n    标记 FETCHING；保持主机源和目的页有效\\\\n    复制完整 A/B、scale 与布局描述；等待真实完成并核对对象与分片\\\\n    成功才发布 READY；失败则不准入该对象的请求\\\\n    失败/取消的在途复制排空后归还预留，不能直接复用目的地址\\\\n\\\\n提交前，为描述、输入、adapter 页和已有状态登记实际读取责任\\\\n将计划与必要就绪依赖一同提交；本轮不再原地改写描述\\\\n\\\\n按模型拓扑逐层推进：\\\\n    取得上一层已经加入 adapter 增量后的输入 X\\\\n    对当前线性层，初始化各行 Y[i] ← W₀ X[i]\\\\n    以当前层对象身份分组，保存每组原始行号列表 J\\\\n    对每组：\\\\n        若该层无增量或 r=0，保留基座结果\\\\n        否则对每个组内行 j 和 k∈[0,r)：\\\\n            U[j,k] ← Σ_t A[k,t] X[J[j],t]\\\\n        确认 U 写入先于其消费者\\\\n        对每个组内行 j 和输出坐标 o：\\\\n            D[j,o] ← s Σ_k B[o,\\\\n\\\\n[EXCERPT extracted-character range 4000:8000]\\\\nr 或已证明的零 padding 决定。这两个量混用会把下一输出行或 padding 当成有效权重。\\\\n\\\\n两阶段执行中，第一阶段按 adapter 组和输入行 tile 分配任务，从 J 收集输入，按页表装入 A 的归约片段，初始化累加器为零，遍历 dᵢ，写出 U。第二阶段按同组的输入行 tile 和输出 tile 分配任务，装入 U 与页表定位的 B，遍历有效 r，再按 J 写回 Y。每个输出坐标由一个任务完整归约时不需要原子加；拆分归约时必须另有归并缓冲和完成关系。prefill 的组有多行，可复用同一权重 tile；decode 常只有一行，更容易受权重 gather、页表访问和启动限制。\\\\n\\\\nS-LoRA 的 MBGMM/MBGMV 支持异 rank、异长度和非连续 gather；论文没有提供足以恢复任意设备 lane、fragment 和矩阵指令布局的信息。本章恢复到逻辑 tile、地址和两阶段依赖，不猜测这些未公开映射，也不据此宣称达到其 CUDA 性能。改用量化权重时，字节寻址之外还需共同定位 scale、分组边界与解码布局。\\\\n\\\\n## 张量并行的数据流与通信口径\\\\n\\\\n以下推导使用列向量、N 个参与者，先假设相关维度可整除 N、同一组具有相同 adapter 版本。传统行向量图的 column/row parallel 名称容易混淆，下面直接说明分片轴。\\\\n\\\\n对于按输出轴分片的线性层，W₀ 的输出行分给各 rank，输入 x 复制。将 A 的 r 行分片为 Aₚ，每个 rank 求 uₚ=Aₚx，all-gather 得到完整 u∈R^r；B 的输出行分片为 Bₚ。各 rank 得到本地输出 W₀,ₚx+sBₚu，与基座输出布局一致。后续按 head 独立计算的 Attention 可继续消费本地输出。此处通信的是低秩 u，而不是完整 dₒ 输出。\\\\n\\\\n对于按输入轴分片的线性层，各 rank 持有 xₚ、W₀,ₚ 和 A 的输入列 Aₚ。先求部分 uₚ=Aₚxₚ，all-reduce 得到 u=Σₚuₚ。B 按输出行分片，每个 rank 求属于其输出区间的 sBₚu。基座部分结果 W₀,ₚxₚ 是完整输出宽度的 partial sum；将本 rank 的增量嵌入对应输出坐标，其余位置补零，再与基座部分结果相加，最后使用基座已有的 all-reduce。这样每个输出坐标的 LoRA 增量恰好加入一次。如果每个 rank 都计算完整 Bu 并在最终 all-reduce 前相加，增量会被重复 N 次。\\\\n\\\\n两层 MLP 中，第一层按输出轴分片，局部非线性后的结果成为第二层按输入轴分片的输入。Q/K/V 与输出投影可使用相应关系，但 GQA、不同投影宽度和不同目标层集合需要重新检查分片，不能从方阵示意图直接推出合法布局。r 不能整除 N 时可选择合法 padding、不同分片或复制，通信和驻留式随之变化。所有参与者还必须确认同一完整对象，不能把 A、B 分别切换版本。\\\\n\\\\nS-LoRA §6 的 Attention 设定包含 Q/K/V 的三个低秩 all-gather 和输出投影的一个低秩 all-reduce。令 Q 为 token 行数、h 为隐藏维，按其环形通信模型，每 rank 发送元素量为：\\\\n\\\\nV_base=2(N−1)Qh/N，V_LoRA=3(N−1)Qr/N+2(N−1)Qr/N=5(N−1)Qr/N。\\\\n\\\\n同一元素字节宽度下，比值为 5r/(2h)；r=16、h=4096 时约 0.00977。N=1 时二者均为零，不计算 0/0。字节量需乘通信 dtype 的元素宽度；全组发送总量再乘 N，不能和单 rank 口径混用。该比值是指定 collective 和融合的数据量关系，不是时间比：小消息启动、拓扑、负载不均及 collective 次数仍可能主导等待。\\\\n\\\\n## 六类成本放在同一资源账中\\\\n\\\\n每个目标矩阵的参数主项为 r(dᵢ+dₒ)b 字节。对组 g 有 Q_g 行、rank r_g，整批基座约为 2Qdᵢdₒ FLOPs，增量约为 Σ_g2Q_gr_g(dᵢ+dₒ)，另有缩放和逐元素相加。补齐执行时用实际执行宽度 R_g 替代 r_g。跨目标矩阵应求和，只有形状相同时才可直接乘矩阵数。\\\\n\\\\n8 个 rank 16 与 8 个 rank 64 的单行请求，实际 rank 位置总数为 640，全补齐到 64 为 1024，低秩部分的维度工作量相差 1.6 倍。基座和 Attention 没有因此减少，不能报告为整个 forward 的 1.6 倍收益。\\\\n\\\\n访存需区分逻辑请求量和设备事务。若某组的 A/B 在本轮各从 HBM 读取一次，增量权重读取主项为 r_g(dᵢ+dₒ)b；多行共享可摊薄该项，多个 tile 重读则增加。显式 U 需要 Q_gr_g 个元素，至少一次写入和一次读取；分支读取 X、对 Y 读改写、行索引和页表也产生流量。逻辑字节不能直接当作 HBM 实测事务：cache 命中、非连续 gather、访存合并、tile 重读和融合会改变它。\\\\n\\\\n驻留按物理页并集计数。一个 adapter 被多个请求引用只计一份设备页，引用责任分别保留。打包对象 i 的字节量为 Dᵢ 时占 ceil(Dᵢ/P) 页；若每个矩阵或 KV 流独立舍入，应求 Σᵢceil(Dᵢ/P)，不能先合并所有字节再舍入。固定槽、空槽、最大 rank padding、量化元数据和旧版本并存都需计入。池内对象不能又与整个已分配池重复相加。\\\\n\\\\n设 64 个 4096×4096 目标矩阵均为 rank 16、两因子 FP16：每矩阵 256 KiB，每 adapter 为 16 MiB。每 token KV 为 128 KiB 时，其有效字节机会成本为 128 token KV。取 P=1 MiB，假设 adapter 已紧密打包，KV 算例只有一条连续逻辑流，公共池为 64 页：一个 adapter 加 384 token 恰占 16+48=64 页；385 token 需 65 页；三个 adapter 加 200 token 需 48+25=73 页。若有多条独立尾流，还要逐流舍入。若将每个 128 KiB 因子独立分配为 1 MiB 页，上述 adapter 容量式也必须重算。\\\\n\\\\n共同池可以借用两类对象的空闲容量；真实固定分池例如 adapter 16 页、KV 48 页，则没有 adapter 时 400 token 的 50 页 KV 会因 KV 分池上限被拒绝，而共同池可容纳。另一种错误是分别允许 adapter 和 KV 各使用 64 页，再称总预算仍是 64 页；这会错误接受前述 73 页需求。前者是合法方案的容量搁置，后者是预算错误。\\\\n\\\\n加载与通信成本由实际路径决定。16 MiB 在有效 16 GiB/s 下的纯 H2D 数据时间为 0.9765625 ms，16 个不同冷 adapter 共 256 MiB，对同一链路为 15.625 ms。文件读取、反序列化、转换、staging 和队列等待另计；主存中的冷对象也受容量与 I/O 约束。预取只有在目的页已预留、预测对象正确且复制真正覆盖等待时才有收益，无用预取仍占带宽和容量。\\\\n\\\\n准备包括行分组、页表构造、图桶选择和描述复制。用哈希分组可在通常假设下以 O(Q) 处理行，用排序则约 O(Q log Q)，不能将其一视为数学必需。同步包括加载完成、U 的生产消费、TP collective、状态发布和最后读取。低秩算术下界、HBM 下界、H2D 下界描述不同资源；可重叠阶段按依赖图求关键路径，不能把它们全部相加或全部取最大而忽略依赖。新旧版本、staging、预取和图缓冲同时存活时决定峰值，不能只列稳态权重与 KV。\\\\n\\\\n## 更新、取消与容量的组合轨迹\\\\n\\\\n以下是设定模型。共同池 64 页，每页 1 MiB；a/v1、a/v2、b/v1 各占 16 页；已有 KV 占 24 页。不含池外基座和执行区，它们已从总设备预算扣除。\\\\n\\\\n| 事件 | 对象与责任 | 容量及允许后继 |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| r1 绑定 a/v1 | a/v1 已就绪，r1 与执行读者保护其页 | a/v1+KV 共 40 页，剩 24 页 |\\\\n| r2 绑定 b/v1，同 token 前缀 | b/v1 另占 16 页，不能命中 a/v1 产生的受影响 KV | 共 56 页，剩 8 页；新增 KV 还须预留 |\\\\n| 发布 a/v2 的制品 | 新请求可以等待 v2，r1 保持 v1 | v2 需 16 页，当前不能直接加载；完整并存需 72 页 |\\\\n| r1 取消，但旧 kernel 未完成 | 撤销新业务提交，实际读者仍存在 | a/v1 的 16 页不能扣掉，容量仍为 56 页 |\\\\n| r2 排空，b/v1 无请求/图引用 | 可撤销 b/v1 驻留并回收 16 页 | 降至 40 页，可预留 v2；加载期间峰值为 56 页 |\\\\n| v2 加载完成并发布 | 新请求绑定 v2，旧 r1 读者仍只读 v1 | 相同 token 的 v1/v2 KV 身份分离 |\\\\n| v1 最后读者完成 | 若所有逻辑/图引用已结束，可回收其权重页 | v1 的缓存 KV 可独立保留；未来 v1 计算仍需重新加载 v1 |\\\\n\\\\n提前把取消视为释放，会在第四行产生虚假容量；原地覆盖 v1 为 v2，会污染旧读者。若 v2 的切流收益不足以承担并存峰值，可以等待旧版排空或使用其他设备；版本更新本身不会创造容量。预取 b/v1 也必须\\\", \\\"excerpt_ranges\\\": [[0, 3083], [4000, 8000]], \\\"related_chapter\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"# K-FW-004：编译与动态形状：Guard、分桶和变体成本\\\\n\\\\n编译把一组可证明成立的执行假设变成专门程序；动态服务需要管理这些假设覆盖的形状与状态空间。\\\\n\\\\n## 特化得到什么\\\\n\\\\n编译器可以融合算子、消除中间张量、选择 tile 和简化控制流，这些改进依赖 shape、stride、dtype、常量或其他 guard。guard 失效可能触发重编译或回退。动态 shape 支持让部分维度符号化，但数据相关控制流、固定 workspace 和特定 kernel 仍可能要求静态边界。\\\\n\\\\nbatch size 相同但 stride 不同、长度分布不同或不同 LoRA rank，都可能走不同变体。只记录一个“batch=8”不足以解释编译缓存。形状签名应描述实际引发特化的条件。\\\\n\\\\n## 分桶的优化目标\\\\n\\\\n将长度 n 映射到桶 b≥n，以 padding 换稳定形状。线性工作浪费近似随 b−n，密集 attention 的浪费则与 b²−n² 有关。bucket 越密，运行浪费越小，但编译时间、可执行程序数量、图和 workspace 驻留越多。\\\\n\\\\n可把总成本写为请求分布下的期望执行成本＋摊销编译成本＋驻留资源代价。某个很少出现的长度值得直接 eager，未必值得专门编译。batch、context、query 数、模态网格是联合维度，对每轴独立细分可能产生组合爆炸。\\\\n\\\\n## 一个分桶推导\\\\n\\\\n假设输入多集中在 100–128 和 900–1024，少量到 2048。只用 2048 桶给短输入造成巨大无效工作；按 128、1024、2048 三桶可能大幅减少它。是否增加 256/512 桶取决于真实分布质量，而非照搬二次幂。前缀命中后待算 query 长度还可能与总历史长完全不同，需要分别考虑。\\\\n\\\\n## 与 CUDA Graph 的关系\\\\n\\\\n编译程序处理算子计算，CUDA Graph 处理一段设备命令的重放。动态编译并不自动使图能改变全部地址和拓扑；固定图也可以调用未编译的 kernel。两者组合时，应先明确编译变体和图桶各自的 key，再说明持久缓冲与有效长度如何输入。\\\\n\\\\n冷启动包括模型加载、编译、autotune、图捕获和内存池建立。稳定态测量可以排除这些成本，部署可用性和首次请求目标则必须包含。重新编译频繁会把所谓稳定服务变成持续冷路径，需从 guard 失效原因推导应符号化还是分桶。\\\\n\\\\n## 从模型函数到 IR、lowering 和执行计划\\\\n\\\\n图获取把某次或一组合法执行的算子与依赖变成中间表示。它必须保留张量 shape、stride、dtype、常量、别名与副作用：写 KV、更新随机状态、通信和事件不能仅当作可任意重排的纯函数。数据相关控制流可能留在宿主、分图或通过受支持表示进入编译；图获取成功不证明所有路径均被覆盖。\\\\n\\\\n图级 IR 描述算子之间的数据流，适合常量折叠、代数改写、融合分组和全局布局传播；算子/循环级 IR 描述每个输出元素的索引、归约域和存储位置，适合 tile、向量化、线程绑定及片上数据复用。Lowering 再把这些计划映射成库调用、目标指令与实际内存操作。TVM 固定论文将计算定义、schedule 和硬件 intrinsic 分开，正是为了让同一函数能有多种合法实现。\\\\n\\\\n编译器可以生成同步与缓冲复用，但其证明范围只覆盖所见依赖。服务执行器仍负责选择变体、提供合法输入、保持在途对象寿命，并协调编译区域外的拷贝、调度和状态提交。将异步 copy 放到另一个 stream，却未将事件关系传入执行计划，不会因模型已经编译而变安全。\\\\n\\\\n## 融合与布局传播需要完整消费者关系\\\\n\\\\n以 Y=activation(XW+b) 为例，GEMM 的 epilogue 可在输出尚在寄存器时完成 bias 与激活，避免中间写读。若未激活的 XW 同时有另一消费者，则要保留该值、复制它或改变融合边界。若归约次序、dtype 或饱和点变化，需验证数值契约；不能只由最终张量 shape 相同判断合法。\\\\n\\\\n把权重预打包成某个内核布局，可在模型加载阶段摊销；运行时激活转换通常按请求付费。一个较快算子若要求额外两次布局转换，可能令整段更慢。图级选择应比较整条 producer→consumer 链，包括 residual 分支、外部库边界、别名和最终输出布局。静态内存复用也必须依据最后消费者，异步执行时不能只按宿主调用返回顺序判定结束。\\\\n\\\\n动态尺寸与动态 rank 需要区别。固定 PyTorch 2026-04-30 文档说明动态 shape 以符号维度描述变化，不支持一般的输入 rank 变化；shape 条件分支仍可产生特化。0/1 等特殊尺寸、stride、数据相关输出数量和自定义 kernel 的 constexpr 也可能影响覆盖范围。标记一个维度动态不会自动解除每个 backend 的静态容量要求。\\\\n\\\\n## 编译缓存与在线变体的实际身份\\\\n\\\\n可执行产物应绑定其真实依赖：算子语义和图、目标架构、编译器/库版本、优化及数值选项、shape/stride/dtype guard 和已折叠常量。若权重只是运行时参数且 ABI/布局不变，不必把每个数值变化都当作重新编译理由；若权重已折叠、预打包格式改变或图捕获保存了地址，则要重建对应产物。缓存失效范围应由依赖决定。\\\\n\\\\n编译、autotune、权重打包和 CUDA Graph 捕获产生不同对象，复用 key 及释放条件也不同。清除编译缓存不代表已实例化 graph 不再引用旧缓冲；更换图桶也不保证旧编译 module 可以立即卸载。新模型版本准备与旧请求 drain 期间，要把两套常量、可执行产物与工作区的并存峰值计入。\\\\n\\\\n一个摊销设定：编译与调优共耗 3 s，每次合法调用节省 0.05 ms，至少需 60,000 次调用才能仅从总计算时间回本；这还未计额外驻留和首请求等待。少见形状可以采用受验证的通用路径，高频形状值得特化。若初始小样本未覆盖长尾，在线不断生成新变体会同时消耗主机与设备资源，应根据实际变体分布重新设计符号范围和桶，而非无限扩大缓存。\\\\n\\\\n## 搜索、回退与验证共同约束编译优化\\\\n\\\\nAnsor 固定论文通过结构草图、细节参数和硬件测量搜索完整张量程序，并把调优预算偏向影响端到端成本的子图。这给 InfraAgents 的设计探索提供一个具体启示：成本模型用于选下一批实验，不能代替合法性与目标硬件测量；局部子图最快也不自动意味着服务尾延迟最佳。\\\\n\\\\n验证至少覆盖 guard 边界内外、非连续输入、别名、特殊尺寸、不同 batch 组成、首次与重复调用，以及更新模型后的缓存命中。保存参考函数并比较分段边界，遇到差异可定位到哪次改写/精度选择。回退路径必须执行相同任务语义，并记录发生条件和占比；静默改变 mask、截断输出或绕开质量约束不属于合法回退。\\\\n\\\\n最终测量包含运行时转换、计划生成、冷编译和长时间变体增长。固定形状、大量复用且融合节省中间流量时，专门编译更有利；高度动态、外部状态多、成熟库已接近瓶颈上限或部署寿命短时，部分编译或直接库调用可能更合适。\\\\n\\\\n<!-- infraagents:provenance -->\\\\n\\\\n## \\\"related_chapter\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"[EXCERPT extracted-character range 4000:7929]\\\\n待状态，不把它们记为本轮已执行。\\\\n   若本轮没有工作，返回 NOOP。\\\\n2. 按实际布局计算 n、全部 query/page 偏移、Q、P 和输出行映射。\\\\n   按签名相容性、每请求上界、整批固定数组容量筛选桶。\\\\n3. 对每个候选在捕获外构造或验证计划：\\\\n   计算有效任务、队列、mask 和部分输出需求；\\\\n   检查每个固定区段上界及捕获的 kernel/grid 契约。\\\\n   计划若改变 kernel 变体，重新选桶，不沿用原候选。\\\\n4. 无候选时，按相容签名和容量拆批，或走相同语义的普通执行；\\\\n   单请求也超界时，仅在模型和服务语义允许时分块，否则回退或拒绝。\\\\n   不截断 query、页表、历史或分支。\\\\n5. 对可行候选估计执行、准备、复制、等待及驻留代价。\\\\n   选择具体 (b,s,E_(b,s))；按槽协议独占取得 s，分配不复用的代次 g。\\\\n   若槽忙则等待、改选或降低并发；等待后重新核对请求快照有效性。\\\\n6. 预留本轮增量状态，检查物理峰值和所有共享状态的读写依赖。\\\\n   槽门控通过后，才把真实输入、偏移、页表和计划写入 A_(b,s)。\\\\n   初始化会被读取的尾部及无效任务标记，登记真实输出行映射。\\\\n7. 令输入、metadata、计划、权重 staging 与 KV 生产完成先于 replay。\\\\n   跨 stream 用相应完成依赖；异步 H2D 的主机源在复制结束前保持不变。\\\\n   成功发布该槽的 (g,ready 依赖,行映射,消费者责任)。\\\\n8. 只启动 E_(b,s)，记录 H=(b,s,E_(b,s),g,映射,完成票据,状态引用)。\\\\n   不允许以“replay b”隐去地址绑定。\\\\n9. 图完成后，消费者按 H 的代次和映射读取输出并提交合法副作用。\\\\n   取消请求抑制业务交付，但仍履行在途完成和清理责任。\\\\n10. 最后消费者结束后释放本轮引用；槽回到可取得状态。\\\\n    host launch 返回不能当作图完成或最后消费者完成。\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n一种确定的拆批方法是先按签名分组，按调度顺序逐个追加请求；追加导致任何实际布局或计划上界越界时，封闭当前合法批，再尝试把该请求放入空批。空批也容纳不了时走单请求回退或拒绝。这是可行的贪心策略，不保证最少批数；每个发出的子批都必须重新建立偏移和映射，并保持完整工作覆盖。\\\\n\\\\n如果填充 s₁ 却启动 `E_(b,s₀)`，图仍会读取 s₀ 并写回其输出地址。即使 s₁ 的内容和代次完全正确，也不能修正这个错误。受支持的节点参数更新或设备间接寻址是其他方案，但必须分别解释如何改变所有相关指针及其在途责任；本章算法不依赖这些替代方案。\\\\n\\\\n## 准备段与固定 grid 的设备数据流\\\\n\\\\n固定 FlashInfer 机制说明把 attention 分成准备和执行。准备消费 query 分段、页索引区间、末页长度、mask 及几何；可能读回长度、打包 mask、选择变体并生成计划。执行消费张量与已准备的 workspace。所给实现的准备段在 host 上运行，不能由该 capture 路径重放；执行段只有满足固定容量及 metadata 保活契约时才可进入图。\\\\n\\\\n源 KV 没变也不意味着计划没变。batch 成员、query 分段、页索引、tail、mask 或变体条件改变，都可能使旧计划失效。同一步的相容层可以复用计划；不同层几何或布局不相容时不能只因处于同一步就共享。\\\\n\\\\n固定 FlashInfer 论文 v1 描述的 v0.2 设计提供了动态任务进入静态图的一条路径：\\\\n\\\\n1. CPU 计划器遍历请求和 query tile，根据其 KV 长度切分任务；用长度与成本估计排序，把任务分配到累计成本较小的 CTA，生成每个 CTA 的有界队列及 partial-to-final 映射。相同输入使用确定的排序和映射。\\\\n2. 计划在 pinned 主机缓冲生成，异步复制到设备 workspace 的固定区段。复制完成先于读取，主机源也在复制结束前受保护。下一代计划不能覆盖上一代仍在读取的源或目标区。\\\\n3. 固定 grid 的持久 attention kernel 从固定队列区读取该代任务数量和描述。每个任务确定 query 行、head、KV 区间及页表区间；CTA 按这些描述读取 Q/K/V，把部分状态写入已分配偏移。无任务 CTA 结束；不能读上一代遗留队列条目。\\\\n4. 对需要切分的同一 query，把互不重叠且完整覆盖可见 key 的部分状态交给 contraction kernel。该 kernel 也用固定 grid，按该代映射读取部分输出，完成归约并写最终行。短 KV 的未切分任务可直接写最终输出，绕过 partial 区和合并。\\\\n5. 真实输出按本轮映射交给消费者；所有 kernel、合并和副作用都使用同一 `(b,s,g)` 的计划。若队列、部分输出或映射超上界，在发布前换方案，不能让 kernel 写出固定区段。\\\\n\\\\n对同一 query 和一致的 score 定义，记分区 I 的 attention 状态为 `(O_I,L_I)`，其中 `L_I=log Σ_{j∈I} exp(score_j)`。两个不相交非空分区的稳定合并为：\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\n算法：合并 attention 部分状态\\\\n若 I 为空，返回 J 的状态；若 J 为空，返回 I 的状态\\\\nm = max(L_I, L_J)\\\\na = exp(L_I - m)\\\\nb = exp(L_J - m)\\\\nO = (a * O_I + b * O_J) / (a + b)\\\\nL = m + log(a + b)\\\\n返回 (O,L)\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n空状态是显式单位元，不能计算负无穷减负无穷。分区若重叠，会重复计权。例如 logits 均为 0、values 为 0 和 2，正确输出是 1；若第二分区重复包含 value 为 0 的位置，错误合并得到 `2/3`。全 mask 行最终如何输出，由 backend 的数值契约决定。\\\\n\\\\n论文按并发请求和累计请求长度为 metadata 各区段建立上界，并在其特定切分及短请求直接写回设计下，给出最多 `2×#CTA` 个 partial tile，每 tile 有 `Tq×Hqo×(D+1)` 个状态元素。换算 bytes 还要分别使用输出与 LSE 的 dtype、对齐和实际布局。本章不把这个上界套给任意切分器；一般计划应按自身任务和合并结构证明容量。\\\\n\\\\n固定 grid 与归约确定性是独立性质。固定切分粒度不保证 launch 的 CTA 数不变；固定 grid 也不保证按完成先后原子合并的结果逐位确定。论文选择确定映射并避免原子聚合，是额外的执行选择。精确算术下的结合律不能变成浮点任意归约树逐位相同。\\\\n\\\\n## 槽位发布、迟到代次与最后消费者\\\\n\\\\n槽 s 初始化为：`phase=FREE`、`gen=-1`、`last_published_gen=-1`、消费者集合为空，绑定地址在图生命期内保持有效。`last_published_gen` 是成功发布代次的高水位，槽变为空闲时也不清零。g 来自不会回退或复用的分配域；迟到事件同时携带槽身份和代次。槽对象销毁后若重建，还需改变槽身份或 epoch，避免旧事件命中新对象。\\\\n\\\\n本章采用一个槽只有一个生产者、全部状态转换由同一拥有者串行化的协议。多生产者实现必须用互斥或等价原子协议保护检查到写入之间的区间，不能分别检查后同时写入。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\n算法 2：固定绑定槽的发布与回收\\\\n输入：槽 s、拟发布代次 g、已验证 payload、消费者责任清单\\\\n\\\\n1. 在槽拥有者的串行域内检查：\\\\n   若 phase ≠ FREE，返回 BUSY，不修改内容、代次或有效完成记录。\\\\n   若 g ≤ last_published_gen，返回 STALE，不修改任何有效内容。\\\\n   独占取得槽，设置 phase=WRITING。\\\\n2. 只向 A_(b,s) 的本轮可写区填充 payload；\\\\n   安排必要复制，保持源与目标在途保护，建立生产到消费的 ready 依赖。\\\\n3. 成功安排完整输入与计划后，一致发布：\\\\n   gen=g；last_published_gen=g；保存映射和 ready 依赖；\\\\n   登记图及后继输出消费者的责任；设置 phase=READY。\\\\n   READY 表示可按依赖提交，不表示 host 已同步等待设备生产完成。\\\\n4. 等待或排入 ready 依赖后启动 E_(b,s)，phase=RUNNING。\\\\n5. 取得该代图完成证据后，结束图责任，phase=DRAINING；\\\\n   输出消费者先取得受保护引用，再读取或复制，完成后逐一结束自己的责任。\\\\n6. 完成通知须匹配槽身份、gen 和尚未结束的责任。\\\\n   旧代、重复或不属于该代的通知不修改当前责任清单。\\\\n7. 图、复制和全部消费者责任都结束后，设置 phase=FREE；\\\\n   保留 last_published_gen，不允许下一代覆盖尚未完成的输出。\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n步骤 1 的拒绝路径发生在任何写入之前。准备阶段若已发出异步写入后失败，槽进入隔离清理状态，不发布部分内容，也不能立即 FREE；待所有已发出访问结束并重新初始化后才恢复可用。失败准备不推进成功发布高水位，但失败操作的代次也不再次分配。\\\\n\\\\n迟到轨迹必须单\\\\n\\\\n[EXCERPT extracted-character range 12000:15154]\\\\n消收益 | 相同 offered workload 比较粗细桶，记录执行行、物理峰值、准入和尾延迟 | 细桶执行更少却可能因驻留导致服务变差，不能只报告 replay 时间 |\\\\n| plan 准备或复制主导 | 固定张量形状，仅改变成员、页表或 mask，分记 plan 与执行 | replay 不变而准备增长，提示准备缓存或表示需要调整 |\\\\n| 共享 workspace 的内容竞争 | 比较独立 workspace 与明确事件串行化，保留相同输入 | 两种方式都消错支持共享区时序解释；仍错误则检查绑定、映射或数值 |\\\\n| 固定 grid 负载不均 | 固定任务集合改变 CTA 数，记录空任务、最长队列和合并时间 | 更多 CTA 只增合并而不缩短关键队列时应停止增加 |\\\\n| 捕获覆盖不足 | 查看整步时间线，调整稳定段的捕获边界 | 图外控制仍留空隙，收益受未捕获关键链限制 |\\\\n\\\\n容量、绑定和迟到代次反例可以用 CPU 离散模型触发。host/device 时间线、stream/event 可见性、真实并发和性能则需要目标设备实验。测量应记录预热、频率、并发、共享带宽和同步点，不能把 host 返回时间或一次 kernel 区间当作完整服务收益。\\\\n\\\\n## 验证范围\\\\n\\\\n随章 `tools/check_k_fw_005_full.py` 是确定、离线、只读的 Python 标准库模型。它用有界数组逐项放置作为独立布局参考，枚举小批容量边界；另外检查固定捕获地址、发布高水位、多消费者门控、旧完成隔离、槽数、填充写入隔离和 attention 合并。故意保留“只逐请求判断”“启动另一槽的图”“不更新高水位”“少一个槽”和“忽略无效行”等负对照，要求它们实际触发不变量失败。\\\\n\\\\n脚本不调用 CUDA，不证明真实 capture 合法性、图更新支持、设备内存可见性、驱动分配或性能。本轮未执行该 Python 文件。真实实现还需核对重复捕获/释放、跨桶切换、超容量回退、取消后迟到事件、权重或 adapter 换入、共享池输出覆盖及峰值存储；设备数值与资源结果应使用独立参考和真实完成记录。\\\\n\\\\n<!-- infraagents:provenance -->\\\\n\\\\n## 来源与推导\\\\n\\\\n- attention、输出投影、残差和本层其余变换，生成下一层 hidden\\\\n10  将本层新 KV scatter 到私有目标槽；不改写共享源前缀\\\\n11 完成全部层、所需 collective 和末行输出；建立消费者可见依赖\\\\n12 核对所有必要 rank 属于同一成功计划，发布长度 L_i 与对应映射\\\\n13 成功后转交持有责任；在最后物理消费者结束后释放 staging 和源保护\\\\n14 任一步失败：禁止发布候选，保留可恢复的旧快照，停止新提交\\\\n15 排空已提交操作后再释放候选页和 staging；取消通知本身不算排空\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n第 3 步可以按层延迟进行，避免同时物化全部层的 flat；这改变暂存峰值和调度，不能省略相应依赖。第 12 步是服务的逻辑发布点，不要求每层或每 token 都做主机全局同步。\\\\n\\\\n若使用输入/输出状态别名，应证明写入范围不会破坏旧提交状态、共享前缀和仍在途的读者。上面的可回退路径依赖私有候选写区；先原地覆盖旧状态，再声称失败时只恢复长度字段，并不能恢复旧内容。完整命中重算末 token 时也一样：共享末页必须隔离写区。\\\\n\\\\n高层 KV 来自本步低层计算得到的 hidden。用原 token、层号或旧高层 KV 直接拼出新位置，会绕过模型计算。检查应比较逐层 KV 与末行输出，最终生成文本相同不足以证明这条数据流正确。\\\\n\\\\n## 生成边界与执行组生命周期\\\\n\\\\ncontext 消费 x[0:L) 后，已完成 KV 长度 p=L，末行 logits 预测位置 L 的 token。采样得到 x_L 后，p 仍为 L；下一次 token generation 消费 x_L，写入 KV[L]，完成后才令 p=L+1。已采样、已交付和已有 KV 必须分别记录。\\\\n\\\\n若下一步消费位置为 p，一维生成桶必须至少容纳 p+1 个位置。桶 1024 表示位置 0…1023：p=1000 或 p=1023 时可用；p=1024 时下一步需要更大桶。超过最大已编译桶时必须报告边界或走另一个受验证路径，不能截断历史。\\\\n\\\\n桶切换保持请求身份、逻辑位置、已确认输入和采样状态。布局相同且共享契约已验证时可以延用状态；布局不同时须先转换；TP 度改变时还需跨 rank 重分布。只更换 executable 名称不会完成这些操作。混合 KV/SSM 模型还需要共同可恢复位置，不能通过截去一个 KV token 推断递归状态也已回到前一步。\\\\n\\\\n执行组从制品校验、权重准备、程序加载、并行组建立、状态/workspace 预留和代表性验证，进入可准入状态。某个 rank 失败时，其他 rank 的局部完成不构成整个请求完成；取消也不能让单个 rank 单独跳过 collective。\\\\n\\\\n新旧版本并存时，旧请求继续绑定旧权重和状态。若容量无法容纳两套程序、权重与在途 KV，应排空或使用其他资源。路由切换不能授权覆盖旧请求仍会读取的地址。预热状态也必须与正式请求隔离。\\\\n\\\\n## 静态张量怎样进入片上计算\\\\n\\\\n固定 NKI 资料给出 Trainium2 的 HBM、SBUF、PSUM、DMA 与专用引擎关系。HBM 与 SBUF 之间主要由 DMA 搬运；PSUM 到 SBUF 则使用计算引擎指令。Tensor Engine 做矩阵计算，Vector/Scalar/GpSimd 承担适合各自能力的归约、逐元素和掩码操作。下面是一条可解释的 attention tile 路径，不宣称 NxD 必定采用该调度。\\\\n\\\\n取 BF16、head 维 d=128、query tile 为 16、key tile 为 128。逻辑 Q 为 [16,128]，K/V 为 [128,128]。QK 的收缩轴是 d，需映射到输入的 partition 轴：Q 以 [128 partition,16 free] 供给 stationary，K 以 [128 partition,128 free] 供给 moving。若 K 在 HBM 中按 [token,d] 连续存放，进入 [d,token] 的 SBUF 时需要实际转置；Trainium2 DMA transpose 可以把源最内层维映射为 partition。\\\\n\\\\nTensor Engine 产生 [16,128] 的 score tile 于 PSUM。计算引擎将分数搬入可处理的缓冲，按绝对 query/key 位置施加 mask，并更新每行在线 softmax 状态。对已有最大值 m、归一化和 ℓ、未归一化输出向量 o，以及本 tile 的合法分数 z，更新为：\\\\n\\\\nm′=max(m,max z)，α=exp(m−m′)，w=exp(z−m′)，\\\\n\\\\nℓ′=αℓ+Σw，o′=αo+wV。\\\\n\\\\n第一块从无有效项状态开始；全无效 tile 直接跳过，避免计算 −∞−(−∞)。最后输出 o/ℓ。概率块若以低精度进入 PV，舍入误差必须纳入数值契约，不能从实数公式推断逐位相同。\\\\n\\\\nPV 的收缩轴是 key：概率转成 [128 partition,16 free] 的 stationary，V 为 [128 partition,128 free] 的 moving，输出累加为 [16,128]。最后再搬至 SBUF，执行后续模型变换并写回 HBM。下一 tile 覆盖缓冲前，必须结束所有仍读取它的引擎操作。\\\\n\\\\n上述 Q、K、V 的有效载荷分别为 4、32、32 KiB；一个 FP32 score tile 为 8 KiB，一个 FP32 输出 tile 为 8 KiB。它们只是分块载荷，不是完整内核的占用证明：在线统计、概率转置、双缓冲、对齐、其他消费者和物理 partition/bank 限制都要按生存期另计。\\\\n\\\\nDMA transpose 竞争 DMA；Tensor Engine transpose 会占用 Tensor Engine/PSUM，并需把结果搬回 SBUF。选择应比较整条消费者链。固定资料还说明硬件 DGE 不支持 indirect gather/scatter，因此不能把外部块表的间接读取自动归为零准备成本的硬件 DGE 路径。\\\\n\\\\n## 计算、交通、准备与驻留的同一份账\\\\n\\\\n对每层、每个 query head，实际有效的因果 query-key 对数为：\\\\n\\\\nP_valid=Σ_i[a_i q_i+q_i(q_i+1)/2]。\\\\n\\\\n若统一 d_k=d_v=d，QK 与 PV 的主 FLOPs 约为 4d×N_layers×H_q×P_valid，另有投影、MLP、归约与采样。重算前缀还增加这些 token 的完整模型计算，不能只计 attention。\\\\n\\\\n桶内因果域的对数为 b_p b_s+b_s(b_s+1)/2；但若矩阵指令先计算\\\\n\\\\n[EXCERPT extracted-character range 8000:12000]\\\\n 分配，还需要 128 MiB 暂存，而有效 900 token 只有 112.5 MiB。源共享块、私有目标、在途快照和 flat 同时存活时应按唯一物理对象计峰值；已预留的页池不能再与池内存活页重复相加。\\\\n\\\\n生成一步的有效 KV 主项随各请求 p_i 增长。只有在权重每步从 HBM 流式读取一次、历史 KV 未命中更近缓存等假设下，才可用 W_r+Σ_i p_iτ_r 作为简化读取模型；当前 token 的新 KV 写入、flat 转换、输出和元数据另计。权重可由 batch 分摊，历史 KV 请求仍依赖各请求长度与 head 复用。该式不是无条件 HBM 下界。\\\\n\\\\n准备包括桶选择、批次归属、块表/slot mapping、描述符、目标预留与权重布局。桶搜索可用有序查找，但请求身份绑定、页数和元数据构建仍有成本。同步包括 DMA 完成、层间依赖、collective、发布和失败排空；逻辑提交不等于额外固定一次全设备同步。\\\\n\\\\n每 rank 的 HBM 峰值应计权重、唯一持久状态、已加载程序/运行时、通信/workspace、flat 和未排空对象。SBUF/PSUM 的活跃 tile 是另一份片上账。固定 NKI 资料的设备级 96 GiB、8 个物理 NeuronCore，以及 NxD 指南在 Trn2 LNC2 下给出的每逻辑 core 24 GB，描述的是不同层级与单位；不能重复相加，也不能把设备总空闲量当作任意 rank 的局部可用量。\\\\n\\\\n固定配置的完整程序族数量可近似记作：\\\\n\\\\nN_prog=Σ_v Σ_batch (|B_s|·|B_p|+|B_tg|)。\\\\n\\\\nv 覆盖实际编译依赖变体；共享、裁剪或其他模型阶段会改变该账。二维组合是两个轴数量的乘积，不能笼统称为随桶数指数增长。新增桶同时增加编译、加载、验证组合与驻留压力。\\\\n\\\\n可用 J=E[T_service]+T_compile/N_use+λM_resident 比较候选，其中时间单位统一为秒/请求，λ 将驻留字节折成同一目标单位。这是带资源权重的策略目标，编译摊销不代表每条请求实际经历该段延迟。T_service 应按真实依赖和共享资源求关键路径，不能把本可重叠的计算、访存和通信全数相加。\\\\n\\\\n## TP、GQA、采样和异步的组合约束\\\\n\\\\n固定指南要求 attention heads 可被 TP 度整除，TP 度还必须属于目标平台支持集合。总权重与 KV 小于组内总内存只是粗必要条件；程序、workspace、复制头和局部峰值仍可能使配置失败。LNC 改变逻辑执行资源与目标编译配置，应共同核对。\\\\n\\\\nGQA 的逻辑头共享不保证 TP 后状态按 TP 度均匀缩小。固定指南提供 REPLICATE_TO_TP_DEGREE 与 CONVERT_TO_MHA：前者通过复制 KV 并调整 Q 对齐，后者把 KV 展开至对应 Q heads；不支持前者配置时，文档描述回退到后者。不能自行用局部 Q/KV 数量之比替代原模型的 head 映射。\\\\n\\\\n设 H_q=32、H_kv=8、TP=16，每 rank 有两个连续 Q heads。每个 KV head 对应四个 Q heads，因而两个相邻 rank 需要同一个 KV head。复制到 TP 度后，每 rank 一份 KV head，全组共 16 份，是逻辑 8 份的两倍。若 32 层、d=128、BF16，逻辑 τ 为 128 KiB/token；每 rank 为 16 KiB/token，1024 token 为 16 MiB，而不是简单除以 16 得到的 8 MiB。若展开到 32 个 KV heads，每 rank 两份，容量还会增加。这是映射算例，不是改变 checkpoint 结构的授权。\\\\n\\\\n增加 TP 可能减少局部权重计算，同时增加 collective 与同步。以行并行线性层为例，每 rank 产生同一输出形状的局部和，需要归并后才能交给后继消费者；其通信载荷随有效/物理 query 数、hidden 维和 dtype 改变。通信是否隐藏取决于依赖、链路和 HBM 争用，不能由更大的 TP 数推断延迟必降。\\\\n\\\\n固定版本 Async mode 的前提是设备端采样；启用投机时还要求 fused speculation。它让 CPU 逻辑与 NEFF 执行重叠，不会消除设备内部依赖或 TP collective。若简化为每步主机准备 t_h、设备执行 t_d，串行约为 t_h+t_d；合法流水在足够多步骤时的间隔下界接近 max(t_h,t_d)，首尾和反馈依赖另计。主机采样需要回传 logits 时，这条重叠假设可能失效。\\\\n\\\\nEAGLE 在该固定指南中特指 v1 flat draft，不支持由此推断任意树形验证。改变采样位置、投机结构或 TP 后，应重新选择合法组合，再比较准备、通信、驻留与质量契约。\\\\n\\\\n## 选择改变、反例与区分实验\\\\n\\\\n前缀命中变短时，应保留长度/位置不变量，重新选择桶并核算有效重算；命中稀疏且转换昂贵时，可以比较关闭缓存。批次组成改变时，必须重新计算共同 suffix 桶及每请求搬移量；逐请求计划不能未经复核直接拼成合批计划。长尾变多时，可增加少量桶或采用较粗通用桶，选择由联合分布与部署复用次数决定。\\\\n\\\\n状态布局或模型身份改变后，只有明确转换可保留旧 KV；改变长度字段不能修复旧字节。异步完成延迟增加后，未排空对象会抬高驻留，应调整准入与预留，而不是提前回收。低流量、部署寿命短或内存紧张时，少量程序与受控排空可能优于大量特化和双版本并存。\\\\n\\\\n反例及实验应能推翻具体解释：\\\\n\\\\n- 把 L 当作 suffix 需求，会把 900/640 请求选到 1024，而正确第一轴为 512。用独立枚举检查最小可容纳 suffix 的桶，再比较最终前缀，不以最终生成文本作为唯一证据。\\\\n- 把零填充历史放进 softmax，会改变分母；给 prefix padding 填入很大的 K/V poison，在保持有效输入不变时，正确输出应不变。若变化只随 poison 出现，优先查 mask，而非先放宽数值容差。\\\\n- 把物理 suffix 偏移 b_p+j 用作绝对位置，会在 b_p≠a_i 时改变位置相关计算。固定输入与 KV，改变物理 padding 容量；正确结果应符合选定数值契约，错误位置路径会随容量变化。\\\\n- 对同一准入请求集比较最小桶和较大桶，分开记录有效工作、实际发射 tile、首次加载和稳定执行。差距只出现在首次调用支持加载解释；稳定差距随物理矩形变化才支持形状执行解释。\\\\n- 固定前缀与 suffix，分别计 gather、attention、scatter 和 flat 峰值，再放开准入。若固定请求集无差距、放开准入后吞吐变化，容量与排队解释优先；若转换阶段随历史增长，应修订仅用命中长度预测收益的模型。\\\\n- 固定模型、输入与设备采样，只改变 Async mode，观察主机空档、NEFF 时间和重叠区间。若 NEFF 本身变慢，先查资源争用或执行配置；若主机空档没有减少，就不能把一次总时间差归因于预期重叠。\\\\n- 在跨桶、单 rank 失败、取消和新旧版本切换处延迟一个真实消费者。检查未完成对象不被重用、失败候选不被发布、旧请求仍绑定旧版本。CPU 事件模型只能反驳错误次序，真实设备的可见性和排空仍需目标实现验证。\\\\n\\\\n随章检查是只读、离线的 Python 标准库 CPU 模型：用独立候选枚举核对二维桶，使用两层标量因果 attention 的完整稠密参考，比较缓存重算后的逐层 KV 与输出，并执行错误总长度选桶、漏 mask、错误物理位置和少计因果对数的负对照。它不加载 NxD，不执行 NEFF，不验证 Neuron/GPU 数值、并发安全、通信和性能；实际执行状态以作者记录为准。\\\\n\\\\n<!-- infraagents:provenance \\\"reading_scope\\\": \\\"full\\\", \\\"category\\\": \\\"related_chapter\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"# K-SYS-002：请求身份：逻辑序列、批次视图与结果归属\\\\n\\\\n请求是长期语义对象，batch 行与物理槽是临时执行位置；正确性依赖它们之间可追溯的映射。\\\\n\\\\n## 身份的四个层次\\\\n\\\\n请求 ID 关联输入和用户输出；序列/分支 ID 关联 beam、投机或多样本；逻辑位置关联 token 历史；执行代次关联某次具体提交。batch index、压紧 token 行和 KV 物理页是这些对象在一轮的视图，不应成为持久身份。\\\\n\\\\n一个请求可参加多个 batch，一个 batch 可包含多个请求，prefill 请求可占多行，投机可产生多条临时分支。分布式 trace 的 parent-child 树并不天然表达所有多对多关系，需要附带执行批与请求贡献映射。\\\\n\\\\n## 压紧和逆映射\\\\n\\\\n假设上一轮顺序为 A、B、C，B 完成后下一轮压紧为 A、C，C 的物理行从 2 变为 1。KV 句柄、length、采样参数、随机状态和输出目标都必须随 C 映射。只移动 token tensor 而其他数组维持原顺序，会把同一行拼成多个请求的混合状态。\\\\n\\\\n变长 prefill 中，请求 A 占 0–127 行，C 占 128 行，末 token logits 的抽取位置与请求级数组又不同。可以用段起止偏移表达这种映射；所有消费者应基于同一轮快照，而非各自重新按当前活跃列表猜测。\\\\n\\\\n## 晚到输出与槽位重用\\\\n\\\\n物理槽重用需要结果携带原请求与代次。旧代次已取消时，业务结果可以丢弃，但其完成仍触发资源释放。若只按 slot 号判断，旧输出可能被当成新请求的第一 token。版本计数帮助区分同一槽的不同生命期。\\\\n\\\\n## 可迁移的实现推导\\\\n\\\\n长期请求状态以稳定身份组织，一轮生成不可变执行视图，执行返回带原映射的结果，再按当前语义状态决定提交、丢弃或回滚。这种分层同样适用于多模态块、分布式子任务和 CPU 小模型。它说明需要什么信息，但不限定具体容器或编程语言。\\\\n\\\\n## 会话、模型版本与恢复代次\\\\n\\\\n会话 ID 连接多轮任务，但一轮请求仍需独立的输入版本、父回合和提交位置；工具等待结束后到达的内容必须归属相应回合。多样本/beam 在请求内产生分支，分支重排改变物理位置而不改变父路径。[分支生成](../algorithms/branch-generation.md) 将这一关系延伸到 grammar、RNG 和 KV 的共同提交。\\\\n\\\\n模型服务别名与具体执行版本也要分开。请求准入时绑定基座、adapter 与 processor 的有效版本；[模型切换](model-lifecycle.md)后，新请求可以使用另一版本，旧请求的身份保持原样。租户作用域还决定同一内容的缓存是否允许共享，不能只凭 token 相同合并拥有者。\\\\n\\\\n迁移会改变执行地点，恢复会改变执行尝试代次，都不应改变已经对外承诺的请求身份。状态包同时携带逻辑恢复点和源/目标的尝试身份；目标只接收与当前授权相容的结果。连接 ID、worker PID 或 slot 号因重试变化，不能成为判定逻辑重复请求的唯一依据。\\\\n\\\\n## 一个贯穿重排、取消和迁移的验证\\\\n\\\\n构造 A、B、C 三请求，其中 B 含两个分支，C 属于另一租户且使用不同 adapter。让 prefill 长度不同、batch 压紧重排、B 淘汰一支、A 取消、C 迁移后原 worker 迟到返回。独立事件账逐次检查“结果行→请求→分支→逻辑位置→模型/adapter→尝试代次”的完整映射。\\\\n\\\\n合法终态应是：A 不再交付新内容但在途资源正常完成；B 只有保留分支更新正式状态；C 只由当前有提交权的代次继续输出，旧结果不进入新 slot。分别核对采样参数、grammar、RNG、KV、计费和 trace 归属，不能用最终文本看起来合理替代身份正确性。\\\\n\\\\n<!-- infraagents:provenance -->\\\\n\\\\n## 来源与推导\\\\n\\\\n- [S-ORCA：Orca: A Distributed Serving System \\\"reading_scope\\\": \\\"full\\\", \\\"category\\\": \\\"source_original\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"=== PDF page 1 ===\\\\nServerlessLLM: Locality-Enhanced Serverless Inference for Large Language Models\\\\nYao Fu1 Leyang Xue1 Yeqi Huang1 Andrei-Octavian Brabete1 Dmitrii Ustiugov2 Yuvraj Patel1 Luo Mai1\\\\n1The University of Edinburgh\\\\n2NTU Singapore\\\\nAbstract\\\\nThis paper presents ServerlessLLM, a locality-enhanced\\\\nserverless inference system for Large Language Models\\\\n(LLMs). ServerlessLLM exploits the substantial capacity and\\\\nbandwidth of storage and memory devices available on GPU\\\\nservers, thereby reducing costly remote checkpoint downloads\\\\nand achieving efficient checkpoint loading. ServerlessLLM\\\\nachieves this through three main contributions: (i) fast LLM\\\\ncheckpoint loading via a novel loading-optimized checkpoint\\\\nformat design, coupled with an efficient multi-tier checkpoint\\\\nloading system; (ii) locality-driven LLM inference with live\\\\nmigration, which allows ServerlessLLM to effectively achieve\\\\nlocality-driven server allocation while preserving the low la-\\\\ntency of ongoing LLM inference; and (iii) locality-aware\\\\nserver allocation, enabling ServerlessLLM to evaluate the sta-\\\\ntus of each server in a cluster and effectively schedule model\\\\nstartup time to capitalize on local checkpoint placement. Our\\\\ncomprehensive experiments, which include microbenchmarks\\\\nand real-world traces, show that ServerlessLLM surpasses\\\\nstate-of-the-art systems by 10 - 200X in latency performance\\\\nwhen running various LLM inference workloads.\\\\n1\\\\nIntroduction\\\\nLarge Language Models (LLMs) have recently been incor-\\\\nporated into various online applications, including program-\\\\nming assistants [23], search engines [16], and conversational\\\\nbots [51]. These applications process user inputs, like ques-\\\\ntions, by breaking them down into tokens (e.g., words). LLMs\\\\nrespond in an autoregressive fashion, predicting each subse-\\\\nquent token based on the combination of input tokens and\\\\nthose generated so far, until a sentence-ending token (EoS) is\\\\nreached. To streamline this process, LLMs employ key-value\\\\ncaches to store intermediate results, reducing the need for\\\\nrepeated computations.\\\\nServing LLM inference at scale is a challenging problem,\\\\ngiven the substantial GPU resources it requires and the low\\\\nresponse time constraints such interactive services need to\\\\nsatisfy. Furthermore, LLM inference latency is difficult to\\\\npredict because their response time depends on the output\\\\nlength, which can vary significantly [24,39,77], due to iter-\\\\native output token generation. To achieve low latency, pro-\\\\ncessing an LLM request often necessitates the use of several\\\\nGPUs for durations ranging from seconds to minutes. In prac-\\\\ntice, LLM service providers need to host a large number of\\\\nLLMs catered to different developers, leading to significant\\\\nGPU consumption [15] and impeding the sustainability of\\\\nLLM services [19]. As a result, LLM inference services have\\\\nto impose strict caps on the number of requests sent to their\\\\nservices from their users (e.g., 40 messages per 3 hours for\\\\nChatGPT [51]), showing the provider’s current inability to\\\\nsatisfy the LLM inference demand. Researchers [19] project\\\\nthat LLM inference costs may increase by > 50× when it\\\\nreaches the popularity of Google Search.\\\\nTo reduce GPU consumption, LLM service providers are\\\\nexploring serverless inference, as seen in systems like Ama-\\\\nzon SageMaker [60], Azure [46], KServe [11] and Hugging-\\\\nFace [31]. In such setup, developers upload their LLM check-\\\\npoints, including model execution files and model parameter\\\\nfiles, to a storage system. Upon receiving a request, the system\\\\nuses a model loading scheduler to allocate available GPUs for\\\\nstarting up these checkpoints. A request router then directs\\\\nthe inference request to the selected GPUs. Using serverless\\\\nmethod enables providers to efficiently multiplex LLMs on\\\\nshared GPUs, enhancing utilization. Additionally, it offers\\\\ncost benefits to the developers, who pay only per request pro-\\\\ncessed, avoiding the expense of long-term GPU reservations.\\\\nWhile serverless inference holds promise for LLMs, it intro-\\\\nduces significant latency overheads. LLM checkpoints, which\\\\nrange from gigabytes [4,72,86] to terabytes [26] in size due to\\\\ntheir significant number of parameters, incur considerable de-\\\\nlays when downloaded from remote storage. Moreover, these\\\\ncheckpoints consist of numerous tensors, each with varying\\\\nstructures and sizes. The process of loading tensors onto\\\\nGPUs (often involving file deserialisation, memory allocation,\\\\ntensor shape parsing, and more) further contributes to delays.\\\\nWe aim to enhance locality in serverless inference for\\\\n1\\\\narXiv:2401.14351v1  [cs.LG]  25 Jan 2024\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 2 ===\\\\nLLMs. Notably, GPU-based inference servers feature multi-\\\\ntier storage architecture which has substantial host memory\\\\nand storage capabilities, yet these resources are underutilized\\\\nin systems like KServe [11] and Ray Serve [68]. Typically,\\\\nonly part of the host memory is used during model inference,\\\\nand SSDs are minimally employed for caching checkpoints\\\\ndownloaded from the model repository. This underutiliza-\\\\ntion led us to a new system design approach: leveraging the\\\\nmulti-tier storage architecture for local checkpoint storage\\\\nand utilizing their significant storage bandwidth for efficient\\\\ncheckpoint loading.\\\\nHowever, this design approach raises several open concerns:\\\\n(i) Given the complex storage architecture of a GPU server,\\\\nwhich includes multiple GPUs, DRAM, SSDs, and remote\\\\nstorage, all interconnected through various connections like\\\\nPCIe, NVMe and networks, how can we optimize LLM check-\\\\npoint loading to fully leverage the available bandwidth? (ii)\\\\nOpting for servers with pre-loaded checkpoints can improve\\\\nlocality in serverless inference systems, but this might cause\\\\nGPU contention because these servers have ongoing LLM\\\\ninferences with unpredictable completion times. How do we\\\\neffectively handle such GPU contention? (iii) In a distributed\\\\ncluster tasked with loading a model for request processing,\\\\nwhat strategy should be employed to select GPUs to minimize\\\\nthe latency of starting up the model?\\\\nTo address the above, we introduce ServerlessLLM, a\\\\nlocality-enhanced serverless inference system for LLMs. We\\\\nmake several contributions in designing ServerlessLLM:\\\\n(1) Fast LLM checkpoint loading. ServerlessLLM can max-\\\\nimize the storage bandwidth usage of GPU servers for LLM\\\\ncheckpoint loading. It introduces (i) a new loading-optimized\\\\ncheckpoint that supports sequential, chunk-based reading and\\\\nefficient tensor in-memory addressing, and (ii) an efficient\\\\nmulti-tier checkpoint loading system that can harness the sub-\\\\nstantial capacity and bandwidth on a multi-tier memory hier-\\\\narchy, through an in-memory data chunk pool, memory-copy-\\\\nefficient data path, and a multi-stage data loading pipeline.\\\\n(2) Locality-driven LLM inference with live migration. We\\\\nmotivate the need for live migration of LLM inference and\\\\nare the first to implement LLM live migration in serverless\\\\ninference systems to enhance the performance when support-\\\\ning locality-driven inference. The live migration is realized\\\\nusing two new mechanisms: (i) efficient token-based migra-\\\\ntion which determines the smallest necessary set of tokens\\\\nfor accurately moving LLM inference to another server, and\\\\n(ii) two-stage live migration enabling the transfer of LLM\\\\ninference without impacting the user experience in online\\\\napplications.\\\\n(3) Locality-aware server allocation. ServerlessLLM aids\\\\nthe model loading scheduler in serverless inference systems\\\\nby enabling latency-preserving, locality-driven server selec-\\\\ntion. It integrates models for accurately estimating the time\\\\nof loading checkpoints from different tiers in the storage hier-\\\\nNode 1 (Warm)\\\\nLLM Instance 1\\\\nController\\\\nInference \\\\nRequest\\\\nKV cache\\\\nRequest \\\\nRouter\\\\nModel \\\\nLoading \\\\nScheduler\\\\nStart-up request\\\\nModel\\\\nStorage\\\\nRoute\\\\nAllocate\\\\nLocal storage\\\\nGPU\\\\nGPU\\\\nNode 2 (Cold)\\\\nLLM Instance 2\\\\nGPU\\\\nGPU\\\\nLocal storage\\\\nLLM\\\\n…\\\\nEOS?\\\\nInput tokens\\\\nOutput tokens\\\\nNext token Yes\\\\nNo\\\\nDownload\\\\nFigure 1: Overview of LLM serverless inference systems\\\\narchy and the time of migrating an LLM inference to another\\\\nserver. Based on the estimation results, ServerlessLLM can\\\\nchoose the best server to minimize model startup latency.\\\\nIn our comprehensive evaluation of ServerlessLLM, we\\\\ncompared it against various baseline methods for running\\\\ndiverse LLM inference workloads in a GPU cluster. Micro-\\\\nbenchmark tests reveal that ServerlessLLM’s rapid LLM\\\\ncheckpoint loading significantly outperforms existing systems\\\\nlike Safetensors [32], and PyTorch [56], achieving 3.6-8.2X\\\\nfaster loading time performance. This is particularly notable\\\\nwith models such as OPT [86], LLaMA-2 [72], and Falcon [4].\\\\nFinally, we evaluated ServerlessLLM with real-world\\\\nserverless\\\\nworkloads, modelled on\\\\nthe\\\\npublic Azure\\\\nTrace [61], and benchmarked it against KServe, Ray Serve,\\\\nand a Ray Serve variant with local checkpoint caching. In\\\\nthese scenarios, ServerlessLLM demonstrated a 10-200X\\\\nimprovement in latency for running OPT model inferences\\\\nacross datasets (i.e., GSM8K [22] and ShareGPT [78]). This\\\\nshows ServerlessLLM’s effectiveness, combining fast check-\\\\npoint loading, efficient inference migration, and optimized\\\\nscheduling for model loading. ServerlessLLM’s source code\\\\nis in progress of releasing at https://github.com/Serve\\\\nrlessLLM/ServerlessLLM.\\\\n2\\\\nBackground and Motivation\\\\n2.1\\\\nServerless LLM Inference\\\\nFigure 1 shows the overview of a serverless LLM infer-\\\\nence system. First, an LLM inference request carries a user-\\\\nspecified input prompt, i.e., a list of tokens, based on which an\\\\ninstance of an LLM service iteratively generates tokens, one\\\\ntoken per iteration, based on the prompt and all the previously\\\\ngenerated tokens, until the end-of-sentence token (denoted\\\\nas EoS) is generated, making the total inference time non-\\\\ndeterministic [39,53]. In each iteration, LLM caches interme-\\\\ndiate computations in a KV cache to speed up the next token\\\\ngeneration [39,54].\\\\nLLM inference services are highly compute and memory-\\\\ncapacity intensive, often requiring many GPUs, the number\\\\nof which needs to be adjusted based on demand, to satisfy\\\\nthe compute and memory-capacity requirements. First, LLMs\\\\nhave a large memory footprint featuring billions of parameters\\\\n2\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 3 ===\\\\n[17,21,26,71,72]. Second, LLM inference often powers up\\\\ninteractive services, often characterized by highly dynamic,\\\\nbursty traffic. The necessity to serve LLM inference requests\\\\nunder strict SLOs at a minimal cost makes LLM inference\\\\nservice scaling a challenge for application developers [14,15].\\\\nTo tackle the LLM inference scaling challenge, cloud\\\\nproviders deploy LLMs as a service, i.e., in a serverless man-\\\\nner where the cloud infrastructure can monitor inference re-\\\\nquest traffic to many LLM inference services deployed in a\\\\nshared cluster of GPUs (or custom inference accelerators).\\\\nIn a typical serverless LLM inference system (as shown in\\\\nFigure 1), the controller that receives inference requests and\\\\ndispatches them to GPU-equipped nodes in a shared cluster\\\\nrunning LLM inference service instances, and cloud storage\\\\nthat hosts model checkpoints.\\\\nThe controller features two components, namely request\\\\nrouter and model loading scheduler. The request router steers\\\\nincoming requests to the nodes already running LLM infer-\\\\nence service instances, further referred as warm nodes, or\\\\nasking the model loading scheduler to spin up more instances\\\\nof the LLM service experiencing a load spike. The model\\\\nloading scheduler allocates nodes from the unallocated, cold\\\\nnode pool to start new LLM service instances. The node se-\\\\nlected by the scheduler launches a new inference process in\\\\na container and initializes the runtime environment. The pro-\\\\ncess then downloads the requested model’s checkpoint from\\\\nthe cloud storage and loads it into the GPU memory.\\\\n2.2\\\\nProblems with Serverless LLM Inference\\\\nA serverless inference cluster can multiplex a large number\\\\nof LLMs on shared GPU servers, showing the promise of\\\\nlargely improving resource utilization and reducing the cost\\\\nof deploying LLMs. This approach benefits from the dynamic\\\\nallocation of resources, allowing for more efficient use of\\\\nGPU servers and potentially lowering user expenses.\\\\nWhile promising, deploying LLMs onto serverless infer-\\\\nence systems often incurs substantial latency overheads. We\\\\nobserved several primary reasons:\\\\n(1) Costly checkpoint download from model repositories.\\\\nServerless functions are designed to separate computation\\\\nand data. AWS, for example, recommends downloading large\\\\ndata from S3 [5,6]. For instance, downloading an LLM check-\\\\npoint with size 130GB (e.g., LLaMA-2-70B [72]) from S3 or\\\\nblob storage takes at least 26 seconds with a fast commodity\\\\nnetwork (5GB/s [14]).\\\\n(2) Costly checkpoint loading from storage devices. Even\\\\nmodel checkpoints can be stored locally in NVMe SSDs,\\\\nloading checkpoints into GPU still takes more than tens of\\\\nseconds (detailed in §7.2). For example, loading OPT-30B\\\\ninto 4 GPUs takes 34 seconds using PyTorch, and LLaMA-\\\\n2-70b into 8 GPUs takes 84 seconds. On the other hand, the\\\\ninference latency per token is around 100ms [41], which is\\\\nsignificantly smaller than the loading latency. Additionally,\\\\nthe startup latency of a serving instance (often a container or\\\\nprocess) often takes several seconds [41], with the potential\\\\nto be further reduced to below a second [42,64,76]. Hence, a\\\\nsignificant component of LLM startup latency is attributed to\\\\nthe loading of a checkpoint.\\\\n2.3\\\\nCurrent Solutions\\\\nTo improve the latency performance when supporting LLMs,\\\\nexisting solutions show a variety of issues:\\\\n(1) Over-subscribing model instances. The existing solu-\\\\ntions [7,79], designed to avoid model download and loading in\\\\na serverless inference cluster, often involve over-subscribing\\\\nGPUs, creating an excessive number of model replicas for\\\\npeak demand. For example, AWS Serverless Inference [7]\\\\ncan keep a certain number of warm instances to mitigate the\\\\neffects of slow cold starts. While this approach is feasible\\\\nfor conventional small models (e.g., ResNet [30]), it becomes\\\\nproblematic for LLMs due to their significantly higher de-\\\\nmand on expensive GPUs.\\\\n(2) Caching models in host memory. Additionally, there are\\\\nsolutions [29,36,83] that maintain model checkpoint caches\\\\nin the host memory of GPU servers, thereby avoiding model\\\\ndownloads. While being effective for conventional small mod-\\\\nels (e.g., up to a couple of GBs [36]) or LoRA adapters [62],\\\\nrelying on a host-memory-based cache only is not sufficient\\\\nfor LLMs. With LLMs, cache misses are common in these\\\\nsystems, resulting in excessive model downloads, and com-\\\\npromising model startup latency (with more details presented\\\\nin §7.4).\\\\n(3) Deploying additional storage servers. There are solu-\\\\ntions [14] advocating for the deployment of additional storage\\\\nservers to cache model checkpoints in a local cluster. How-\\\\never, recent trace studies [14] have revealed that download-\\\\ning a model can take over 20 seconds through an optimized\\\\npipeline connected to local commodity storage servers, even\\\\nif it is equipped with a 100 Gbps NIC. While the further\\\\nadoption of high-speed networks (e.g., 200 Gbps Ethernet or\\\\nInfiniBand) can reduce this latency, the cost of deploying the\\\\nadditional storage servers and high-bandwidth networks often\\\\nincurs formidable expenses [13,28].\\\\n3\\\\nLocality-Enhanced Serverless Inference\\\\nWe now introduce ServerlessLLM – a novel low-latency\\\\nserverless inference system designed for LLMs. Serverless-\\\\nLLM addresses the two issues we highlighted in the previous\\\\nsection – very high model download time and inefficient load-\\\\ning the model into the GPU memory from the local storage.\\\\nOur design is motivated by a simple observation that GPU-\\\\nbased servers used for inference incorporate a multi-tier stor-\\\\nage hierarchy having substantial capacity and bandwidth.\\\\n3\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 4 ===\\\\nFrom a capacity perspective, GPU servers are integrated with\\\\nsubstantial memory capabilities, hosting terabyte-scale mem-\\\\nory, tens of terabytes in NVMe SSDs, and up to hundreds of\\\\nterabytes in SATA SSDs [49]. From a bandwidth perspective,\\\\nGPU servers often comprise several GPUs, each connected to\\\\nthe host memory via a dedicated PCIe link. Similarly, NVMe\\\\nSSDs also connect via their own PCIe channels. For instance,\\\\nan 8-GPU server with PCIe 4.0 offers 256GB/s bandwidth be-\\\\ntween host memory and GPU, and 10-30 GB/s between host\\\\nmemory and NVMe SSD (in RAID 0). The Grace-Hopper\\\\narchitecture improves CPU-GPU bandwidth to 900GB/s [48].\\\\nAdditionally, we observe that in serverless inference context, a\\\\nsignificant portion of the GPU servers’ host memory and stor-\\\\nage devices are under-utilized, leaving a significant portion\\\\nof the bandwidth and capacity unused.\\\\nBased on the above observation, we want to explore\\\\nlocality-enhanced serverless inference for LLMs where the\\\\nsystem exploits the unused capacity and bandwidth to store\\\\nthe models locally and load the models faster, thereby reduc-\\\\ning the latency. In realizing our design, we anticipate three\\\\nimportant concerns that our design should consider.\\\\n(1) Multi-tiered storage hierarchy support. Existing check-\\\\npoint and model loaders such as PyTorch [56], Tensor-\\\\nFlow [70], and ONNX Runtime [59] primarily focus on fa-\\\\ncilitating the training and debugging of models. However,\\\\nthese tools are not optimized for reading performance, which\\\\nbecomes a significant issue in a serverless inference environ-\\\\nment. In such environments, model checkpoints are stored\\\\nonce but need to be loaded and accessed repeatedly across\\\\nmultiple GPUs. This lack of optimization for read opera-\\\\ntions leads to substantial loading delays, impacting overall\\\\nefficiency. Solutions such as Safetensors [32] can improve\\\\nloading performance. However, as we show in Section 7,\\\\nthey still do not exploit the full potential of the multi-tiered\\\\nmemory hierarchy. ServerlessLLM design needs to consider\\\\nperformance as a key aspect such that it can harness the entire\\\\nmemory hierarchy’s capacity and bandwidth efficiently. To ad-\\\\ndress the concern, we discuss the design of loading optimized\\\\ncheckpoints and the model manager in Section 4.\\\\n(2) Strong locality-driven inference. Designing an efficient\\\\nmodel loader is not enough; one needs to have a central entity\\\\nthat can recognize the checkpoint placements and the current\\\\nload on each GPU server to enhance locality-driven inference.\\\\nExisting serverless systems randomly assign models to avail-\\\\nable GPUs overlooking the locality factor. Despite cluster\\\\nscheduling systems such as Sparrow [52] focusing on locality\\\\noptimization, they cause significant queueing delays if the\\\\nassigned GPU is busy. Distributed model serving systems\\\\n(such as ClockWork [29] and Shepherd [85]) can consider\\\\nlocality. They however either rely on the accurate prediction\\\\nof model inference time, making them struggle with LLMs, or\\\\nthey preempt ongoing model inferences, leading to significant\\\\ndowntime and redundant computations. Hence, Serverless-\\\\nLLM needs to accommodate a new approach that prioritizes\\\\ncheckpoint locality while avoiding interrupting ongoing LLM\\\\ninference. We discuss the design of such an approach in Sec-\\\\ntion 5.\\\\n(3) Resource allocation optimized for locality. Serverless-\\\\nLLM is designed to minimize the model startup latency by\\\\nleveraging the local checkpoint placement. The model load-\\\\ning scheduler plays a crucial role in allocating GPU resources\\\\nto achieve that goal. However, the scheduler needs to allocate\\\\nresources after careful consideration of the entire cluster sta-\\\\ntus. Many factors may influence the overall startup latency,\\\\nsuch as the difference in the bandwidth offered by each layer\\\\nin the memory hierarchy. There may be instances where it is\\\\nbeneficial to move the current inference execution to a new\\\\nGPU than to allocate the request to a GPU where the model\\\\nmay have to be loaded from the storage media. Hence, Server-\\\\nlessLLM needs to accurately estimate the startup times con-\\\\nsidering the cluster status and accordingly allocate resources\\\\nto minimize startup time. We discuss the design of such a\\\\nstartup-time-optimized allocation approach in Section 6.\\\\nSummary. ServerlessLLM ensures that the model loading\\\\ntime is minimal to improve the overall latency by harnessing\\\\nthe memory and storage capacity and bandwidth available on\\\\nthe local GPU. The model manager we describe next handles\\\\nefficient loading of the checkpoints. ServerlessLLM relies on\\\\nthe modified scheduler to ensure that the inference requests\\\\nare assigned to those GPUs that already have the model data\\\\nstored locally to avoid downloading.\\\\n4\\\\nFast LLM Checkpoint Loading\\\\nWe create loading-optimized checkpoints for efficient loading\\\\nwith a model manager and further enhance performance with\\\\nan efficient multi-tier checkpoint storage system.\\\\n4.1\\\\nLoading-Optimized Checkpoints\\\\nWe operate under a set of assumptions about the checkpoints.\\\\nThe checkpoints have: (i) Model execution files which de-\\\\nfine the model architecture. Depending on the framework, the\\\\nformat varies; TensorFlow typically uses protobuf files [69],\\\\nwhile PyTorch employs Python scripts [55]. Beyond architec-\\\\nture, these files detail the size and shape of each tensor and\\\\ninclude a model parallelism plan. This plan specifies the target\\\\nGPU for each tensor during checkpoint loading. (ii) Model\\\\nparameter files which stores the binary data of parameters in\\\\nan LLM. Tensors within these files can be arranged in any\\\\nsequence. Runtimes such as PyTorch may also store tensor\\\\nshapes as indices to calculate the offset and size for each\\\\ntensor.\\\\nServerlessLLM converts the given checkpoint into a new\\\\nloading-optimized format. The conversion has two primary\\\\ngoals: (i) Support sequential chunk-based reading: To ensure\\\\n4\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 5 ===\\\\nGPU\\\\nInference Process\\\\nModel Manager\\\\nModel execution files\\\\nGPU\\\\n(model name, GPU ids)\\\\nSynchronisation\\\\n2\\\\n1\\\\nModel\\\\nInitialization \\\\nFunction\\\\nBinary Data\\\\nTensor index file\\\\nTensor data files\\\\nBase address\\\\nGPU 0\\\\nBase address\\\\nGPU 1\\\\nLoading-optimised checkpoint\\\\n<GPU id, base address>\\\\nModel\\\\nDefinition\\\\nLoading\\\\nFunction\\\\n<tensor.name, GPU id, offset, size>\\\\nModel Object\\\\nInitialized\\\\nModel Object\\\\nIssue loading to GPU\\\\nFigure 2: Checkpoint loading process.\\\\nefficient sequential reading, tensors for each GPU are grouped\\\\nin separate files. These files contain only the binary data of\\\\nmodel parameters and exclude metadata such as tensor shapes,\\\\nfacilitating large chunk reading. (ii) Support efficient tensor\\\\naddressing: We create an index file that maps tensor names\\\\nto a tuple of GPU id, offset, and size, facilitating the efficient\\\\nrestoration of tensors. The tensors are aligned with memory\\\\nword sizes, facilitating direct computation of memory address\\\\nand avoiding deserialization.\\\\nServerlessLLM has an in-server model manager to load\\\\nthe loading-optimized checkpoints. The loading process is\\\\nillustrated in Figure 2. ServerlessLLM model manager al-\\\\nlocates memory on GPUs and preloads the binary data of\\\\nthe checkpoints (see 1 ). The preloading operation can ben-\\\\nefit from the sequential chunk-based read design. While the\\\\nmodel is needed, the inference process can efficiently obtain\\\\nthe memory address of the checkpoints in the GPU (see 2 ).\\\\nSpecifically, ServerlessLLM provides a loading function for\\\\nLLM libraries. This function acquires the base addresses for\\\\neach GPU (i.e., CUDA IPC handles). By querying the tensor\\\\nindex file, this function iterates through the model and set\\\\neach tensor’s memory address (i.e., base + offset). To ensure\\\\nthe model is fully initialized before inference, the inference\\\\nprocess and the model manager perform a synchronization.\\\\n4.2\\\\nEfficient Multi-Tier Checkpoint Loading\\\\nTo boost the checkpoint loading, we design an efficient\\\\nmulti-tier checkpoint loading subsystem, integrated within\\\\nthe model manager. This subsystem incorporates several tech-\\\\nniques:\\\\nIn-memory data chunk pool. We’ve developed an in-\\\\nmemory data chunk pool in ServerlessLLM with three main\\\\ngoals: (i) Utilizing parallel PCIe links. To mitigate the bottle-\\\\nneck caused by a single PCIe link from storage when loading\\\\nmultiple models into GPUs, we employ parallel DRAM-to-\\\\nGPU PCIe links to facilitate concurrent checkpoint loading\\\\nacross GPUs. (ii) Supporting application-specific controls.\\\\nOur memory pool surpasses simple caching by providing\\\\nAPIs for the allocation and deallocation of memory. This\\\\nenables fine-grained management of cached or evicted data\\\\nchunks, based on specific requirements of the application.\\\\n(iii) Mitigating memory fragmentation. We address latency\\\\nand space inefficiencies caused by memory fragmentation by\\\\nusing fixed-size memory chunks for allocation and dealloca-\\\\ntion.\\\\nEfficient data path. We’ve created an efficient data path in\\\\nour model manager with two main strategies: (i) Exploiting\\\\ndirect file access. We use direct file access (e.g., ‘O_DIRECT’\\\\nin Linux) to avoid excessive data copying by directly read-\\\\ning data into user space. This method outperforms memory-\\\\nmapped files (mmap), currently adopted in high-speed loaders\\\\nsuch as Safetensors [32], which rely on system cache and lack\\\\nconsistent performance guarantees (critical for low latency\\\\nscenarios). (ii) Exploiting pinned memory. We utilize pinned\\\\nmemory to eliminate redundant data copying between DRAM\\\\nand GPU. This approach allows direct copying to the GPU\\\\nwith minimal CPU involvement, ensuring efficient use of PCIe\\\\nbandwidth with a single thread.\\\\nMulti-stage data loading pipeline. We accommodate a multi-\\\\nstage data loading pipeline to maximize throughput: (i) Sup-\\\\nport for multiple storage interfaces. ServerlessLLM offers\\\\ndedicated function calls for various storage interfaces, includ-\\\\ning local storage (e.g., NVMe, SATA), remote storage (e.g.,\\\\nS3 object store [5]), and in-memory storage (pinned mem-\\\\nory). It utilizes appropriate methods for efficient data access\\\\nin each case. (ii) Optimization for intra-stage throughput. To\\\\nleverage modern storage devices’ high concurrency, Server-\\\\nlessLLM employs multiple threads for reading data within\\\\neach storage tier, improving bandwidth utilization. (iii) Ef-\\\\nficient inter-stage coordination. ServerlessLLM uses a task\\\\nqueue-based pipeline for extensibility and low latency. Load-\\\\ning threads read storage chunks and enqueue their indices\\\\n(offset and size) for the loading threads in the next tier.\\\\n5\\\\nLocality-Driven LLM Inference\\\\nwith Live Migration\\\\nIn this section, we describe how ServerlessLLM achieves\\\\nlive migration for LLM inference, which enables locality-\\\\ndriven model startup while avoiding affecting ongoing LLM\\\\ninference.\\\\n5.1\\\\nNeed for Live Migration\\\\nWe consider a simple example to analyze the performance\\\\nof different current approaches in supporting the checkpoint\\\\nlocality. In this example, we have two servers (named Server\\\\n1 and Server 2) and two models (named Model A and Model\\\\nB), as illustrated in Figure 3. Server 1 currently has Model\\\\nA in DRAM and Model B in SSD and its GPU is idle, while\\\\nServer 2 currently has Model B in DRAM, and its GPU is\\\\nrunning the inference of Model A.\\\\nIn Figure 3, we analyze the performance of potential poli-\\\\ncies for starting up Model B. Our analysis is based on their\\\\n5\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 6 ===\\\\nS1\\\\nLoad B\\\\nS2\\\\nInfer A\\\\nInfer B\\\\n(a) Availability-driven policy\\\\nS1\\\\nS2\\\\nInfer A\\\\nLoad B\\\\nInfer B\\\\n(b) Locality-driven policy\\\\nS1\\\\nS2\\\\nInfer A\\\\nLoad B\\\\nInfer B\\\\nLoad A\\\\n(c) Preemption-driven policy\\\\nS1\\\\nS2\\\\nInfer A\\\\nLoad B\\\\nInfer B\\\\nInfer A\\\\n(d) Live-migration-supported locality-driven policy\\\\nTimeline\\\\nRequest to start up model B\\\\nLoad A\\\\nRecompute A\\\\nInfer A\\\\nServer 1 (S1)\\\\nGPU\\\\nDRAM\\\\nSSD\\\\nModel A\\\\nModel B\\\\nServer 2 (S2)\\\\nGPU\\\\nDRAM\\\\nSSD\\\\nModel A\\\\nModel B\\\\nSetup\\\\nPerformance\\\\nLong interruption time\\\\nLive migration\\\\nA Latency:\\\\nB Latency:\\\\nA Latency:\\\\nB Latency:\\\\nA Latency:\\\\nB Latency:\\\\nA Latency:\\\\nB Latency:\\\\nFigure 3: Analysis of different locality-driven policies\\\\nimpact on the latency performance of both Model A and B:\\\\n• Availability-driven policy chooses Server 1 currently with\\\\nan available GPU, and it is agnostic to the location of Model\\\\nB. As a result, the Model B’s startup latency suffers while\\\\nthe Model A remains unaffected.\\\\n• Locality-driven policy opts for the locality in choosing the\\\\nserver and thus launching Model B on Server 2. However,\\\\nit waits for Model A to complete, making Model B suffer\\\\nfrom a long queuing delay. Furthermore, the locality policy\\\\nleaves Server 1 under-utilized, preventing all servers from\\\\nbeing fully utilized.\\\\n• Preemption-driven policy preempts Model A on Server 2\\\\nand startups Model B. It identifies that Server 1 is free and\\\\nreinitiates Model A there. This policy reduces Model B’s\\\\nlatency but results in significant downtime for Model A\\\\nwhen it performs reloading and recomputation.\\\\n• Live-migration-supported locality-driven policy prioritizes\\\\nlocality without disrupting Model A. It initially preloads\\\\nModel A on Server 1, maintaining inference operations.\\\\nWhen Model A is set on Server 1, its intermediate state\\\\nis transferred there, continuing the inference seamlessly.\\\\nFollowing this, Model B commences on Server 2, taking\\\\nadvantage of locality. This policy optimizes latency for both\\\\nModels A and B.\\\\nAs we can see, among the policies for enhancing locality,\\\\nlive migration stands out in effectively improving latency for\\\\nboth Model A and Model B.\\\\n5.2\\\\nLive Migration Process\\\\nIn designing live migration for LLM inference, we first looked\\\\nat the standard method: snapshotting the LLM inference and\\\\nmigrating it (similar to Singularity [66]). Yet, this approach\\\\nLoad(Model A)\\\\nMigrate(Dest)\\\\n1\\\\n2\\\\n3\\\\n5\\\\nRequest \\\\nRouter\\\\nLoading \\\\nScheduler\\\\nSource \\\\nServer\\\\nDestination \\\\nServer\\\\n(\\\\\\\"migrated\\\\\\\", Dest, all tokens)\\\\n4\\\\n6\\\\n7\\\\nContinue inference with all tokens\\\\nResume \\\\nintermediate tokens\\\\nMigration \\\\ntime\\\\nMigration \\\\nimpact\\\\nTime\\\\nFigure 4: Live migration process for LLM inference\\\\nhas notable downsides: snapshot creation and transfer are\\\\nslow (taking tens of seconds [66]), as they encompass the\\\\nmodel checkpoint, runtime states (input tokens, KV cache),\\\\nand extensive GPU state.\\\\nTo address the above, we propose token-based migration.\\\\nOur proposal is based on the following insight: during infer-\\\\nence, the model checkpoint is read-only, and the KV cache\\\\ncan be recalculated from tokens with low latency, usually in\\\\nthe range of hundreds of milliseconds. Thus, if a copy of the\\\\nmodel checkpoint exists on another server, we can initiate the\\\\nmodel there and then transmit all current tokens. This way, the\\\\nonly state transferred over the network is a list of tokens (i.e.,\\\\nan int64 array). Even with a large batch size (64) and long\\\\nsequence (e.g., 100k tokens for long context LLM [9]), the\\\\ntoken size remains in the scale of MBs, significantly smaller\\\\nthan the typical sizes of the KV cache (e.g., GBs) and check-\\\\npoints (e.g., tens of GBs).\\\\nTo avoid interrupting inference while migrating tokens,\\\\nwe designed a two-stage process. In stage 1, the destination\\\\nserver (referred to as the dest server) recalculates the KV\\\\ncache using the intermediate tokens. Then, in stage 2, the dest\\\\nserver receives the remaining tokens that were produced after\\\\nthe intermediate tokens were sent. This two-stage process is\\\\ndepicted in Figure 4 with its steps described below:\\\\n1. The model loading scheduler sends a model loading re-\\\\nquest to dest server to load model A into GPUs. If there is\\\\nan idle instance of model A on dest server, the scheduler\\\\nskips this step.\\\\n2. After loading, the scheduler sends a migration request\\\\ncarrying the address of dest server to src server.\\\\n3. Upon receiving a migrate request, src server sets itself\\\\nas “migrating”, sends a resume request with intermediate\\\\ntokens (i.e., input tokens and the output tokens produced\\\\nbefore step 3) to dest server if the inference is not com-\\\\npleted. Otherwise, it immediately returns to the scheduler.\\\\n4. dest server recomputes KV cache given the tokens in the\\\\nresume request.\\\\n5. Once resume request is done, src server stops inference,\\\\n6\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 7 ===\\\\nreturns to the scheduler, and replies to the request router\\\\nwith all tokens (i.e., the intermediate tokens together with\\\\nthe remaining tokens produced between step 3 and step 5)\\\\nand a flag “migrated”. If long-context, the collection of all\\\\ntokens can be very large thus resuming takes a long time,\\\\nduring which many new tokens are predicted. In such a\\\\ncase, we can repeat the above two steps to further reduce\\\\nthe tokens to send between src and dest.\\\\n6. The scheduler finishes the migration, unloads model A at\\\\nsrc server and starts loading model B.\\\\n7. The request router checks the flag in the inference response.\\\\nIf it is “migrated”, the request router replaces src server\\\\nwith dest server in its route table and sends all tokens to\\\\ndest server to continue inference.\\\\n5.3\\\\nPractical Concerns\\\\nHandling inference completion. The autoregressive nature\\\\nof LLM inference may lead to task completion at src server\\\\nbetween steps 3 and 5 . In such cases, src server informs the\\\\nrequest router of the inference completion as usual. Addition-\\\\nally, it notifies the loading scheduler, which then instructs dest\\\\nserver to cease resuming, terminating the migration.\\\\nHandling server failures. ServerlessLLM can manage server\\\\nfailures during LLM inference migration. In scenarios where\\\\nsrc server fails, if the failure happens during loading (i.e.,\\\\nbefore step 2 in Figure 4), the scheduler aborts the migration\\\\nand unloads the model from the destination. If the failure\\\\noccurs during migration (i.e., between steps 2 and 3 ), the\\\\nscheduler directs the destination to clear any resumed KV\\\\ncache and unload the model.\\\\nAdditionally, in cases where src server fails, if the failure\\\\ntakes place during loading, the migration is canceled by the\\\\nscheduler. Should the failure occur while resuming, the source\\\\nnotifies the scheduler of the failure and continues with the\\\\ninference.\\\\n6\\\\nLocality-Aware Server Allocation\\\\nIn this section, we describe the details of achieving the\\\\nlocality-aware allocation of servers when scheduling a model\\\\nto startup. The scheduler incorporates estimators for model\\\\nloading time and model migration time to choose the best\\\\nserver depending on the status of each server.\\\\n6.1\\\\nModel Loading Scheduler Design\\\\nFigure 5 introduces the model loading scheduler in Server-\\\\nlessLLM. The scheduler processes loading tasks from the\\\\nrequest router and employs two key components: a model\\\\nloading time estimator and a model migration time estima-\\\\ntor. The former assesses loading times from various storage\\\\nmedia, while the latter estimates times for necessary model\\\\nController\\\\nRequest Router\\\\nServerlessLLM Model Loading \\\\nScheduler\\\\nServer 3\\\\nGPU\\\\nDRAM\\\\nSSD\\\\nModel A\\\\nA\\\\nServer 2\\\\nGPU\\\\nDRAM\\\\nSSD\\\\nModel B\\\\nB\\\\nModel A\\\\nA\\\\nServer 1\\\\nGPU\\\\nDRAM\\\\nSSD\\\\nModel B\\\\nModel C\\\\nB\\\\nReliable Key-Value Store\\\\nModel Loading \\\\nTime Estimator\\\\nModel Migration \\\\nTime Estimator\\\\nModel Loading Task Queues\\\\nInference \\\\nRequest\\\\nInference \\\\nRequest\\\\nLoading \\\\nTask\\\\nLoading \\\\nTask\\\\nServer \\\\nStatus\\\\nGPU \\\\nStatus\\\\nDRAM & \\\\nSSD Status\\\\nLoading \\\\nResults\\\\nLoading \\\\nResults\\\\nInference \\\\nStatus\\\\nServer Task Queue\\\\nFigure 5: Model loading scheduler design\\\\nmigrations. For example, as shown in Figure 5, the scheduler\\\\ncalculates the time to load Model A (indicated by A ) from\\\\ndifferent servers’ DRAM and SSD, aiding in server selection.\\\\nSimilarly, for Model B ( B ), it assesses whether to migrate\\\\nModel C to another server or load Model B from Server 2’s\\\\nSSD.\\\\nTo enhance accuracy, the ServerlessLLM scheduler main-\\\\ntains distinct loading task queues per server. Upon assigning a\\\\ntask, it updates server status, including GPU and DRAM/SSD\\\\nstates, in a reliable key-value store (e.g., etcd [27] and\\\\nzookeeper [34]), allowing ServerlessLLM to recover from\\\\nfailures.\\\\n6.2\\\\nEstimating Model Loading Time\\\\nTo estimate the time needed to load models from different\\\\nstorage tiers, we consider three primary factors: (i) queuing\\\\ntime (q), which is the wait time for a model in the server’s\\\\nloading task queue. This occurs when other models are pend-\\\\ning load on the same server; (ii) model size (n), the size of the\\\\nmodel in bytes, or its model partition in multi-GPU inference\\\\nscenarios; (iii) bandwidth (b), the available speed for transfer-\\\\nring the model from storage to GPUs. ServerlessLLM tracks\\\\nbandwidth for network, SSD, and DRAM, allowing us to cal-\\\\nculate loading time as q + n/b. Here, q accumulates from\\\\nprevious estimations for the models already in the queue.\\\\nFor precise estimations, we have implemented: (i) Sequen-\\\\ntial model loading per server, with single I/O queues for both\\\\nSSD-memory and network-memory, reducing bandwidth con-\\\\ntention which complicates estimation; (ii) In multi-tier stor-\\\\nage, ServerlessLLM uses the slowest bandwidth for estima-\\\\ntion because of ServerlessLLM’s pipeline loading design. For\\\\nexample, when SSD and DRAM are both involved, SSD band-\\\\nwidth is the critical bottleneck since it is orders of magnitude\\\\n7\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 8 ===\\\\nslower than DRAM; (iii) The scheduler monitors the loading\\\\nlatency returned by the servers. It leverages the monitoring\\\\nmetrics to continuously improve its estimation of the band-\\\\nwidth through different storage media.\\\\n6.3\\\\nEstimating Model Migration Time\\\\nFor live migration time estimation, our focus is on model\\\\nresuming time (as shown in step 4 in Figure 4), as this is\\\\nsignificantly slower (seconds) than token transfer over the\\\\nnetwork (milliseconds). We calculate model resuming time\\\\nconsidering: (i) input tokens (tin), the number of tokens in\\\\nthe LLM’s input prompt; (ii) output tokens (tout), the tokens\\\\ngenerated so far; and (iii) model-specific parameters (a and\\\\nb), which vary with each LLM’s batch sizes and other factors,\\\\nbased on LLM system studies like vLLM [39]. With all the\\\\nabove factors, we can compute the model resuming time as\\\\na×(tin +tout)+b.\\\\nHowever, obtaining real-time output tokens from servers\\\\nfor the scheduler can lead to bottlenecks due to exces-\\\\nsive server interactions. To circumvent this, we developed\\\\na method where the scheduler queries the local request router\\\\nfor the inference status of a model, as illustrated in Figure 5.\\\\nWith the inference duration (d) and the average time to pro-\\\\nduce a token (t), we calculate tout = d/t.\\\\nFor selecting the optimal server for model migration,\\\\nServerlessLLM employs a dynamic programming approach\\\\nto minimize migration time.\\\\n6.4\\\\nPractical Concerns\\\\nSelecting best servers. Utilizing our time estimation tech-\\\\nniques, ServerlessLLM evaluates all servers for loading the\\\\nforthcoming model, selecting the one offering the lowest es-\\\\ntimated startup time. The selection includes the server ID\\\\nand GPU slots to assign. If no GPUs are available, even after\\\\nconsidering migration, the loading task is held pending and\\\\nretried once the request router informs the scheduler to release\\\\nGPUs.\\\\nHandling scheduler failures. ServerlessLLM is built to with-\\\\nstand failures, utilizing a reliable key-value store to track\\\\nserver statuses. On receiving a server loading task, its GPU\\\\nstatus is promptly updated in this store. Post server’s confir-\\\\nmation of task completion, the scheduler updates the server’s\\\\nstorage status in the store. Once recorded, the scheduler no-\\\\ntifies the request router of the completion, enabling request\\\\nrouting to the server. In the event of a scheduler failure, re-\\\\ncovery involves retrieving the latest server status from the\\\\nkey-value store and synchronizing it across all servers.\\\\nScaling schedulers. The performance of the loading sched-\\\\nuler has been significantly enhanced by implementing asyn-\\\\nchronous operations for server status reads, writes, and esti-\\\\nmations. Current benchmarks demonstrate its capability to\\\\nTable 1: Details of models used in cluster evaluation.\\\\nName\\\\nSize (GB)\\\\n# Required GPUs\\\\n# Instances\\\\nOPT-6.7B\\\\n13.3\\\\n1\\\\n32\\\\nOPT-13B\\\\n25.7\\\\n2\\\\n16\\\\nOPT-30B\\\\n60\\\\n4\\\\n8\\\\nhandle thousands of loading tasks per second on a standard\\\\nserver. Plans for its distributed scaling are earmarked for fu-\\\\nture development.\\\\nResource fairness. ServerlessLLM treats all models with\\\\nequal importance and it ensures migrations do not impact\\\\nlatency. While we currently adopt sequential model loading\\\\non the I/O path, exploring concurrent loading on servers with\\\\na fairness guarantee is planned for future work.\\\\nEstimator accuracy. Our estimator can continuously improve\\\\ntheir estimation based on the monitored loading metrics re-\\\\nturned by the servers. They offer sufficient accuracy for server\\\\nselection, as shown in Section 7.\\\\n7\\\\nEvaluation\\\\nThis section offers a comprehensive evaluation of Server-\\\\nlessLLM, covering three key aspects: (i) assessing the per-\\\\nformance of our loading-optimized checkpoints and model\\\\nmanager, (ii) examining the efficiency and overheads associ-\\\\nated with live migration for LLM inference, and (iii) evaluat-\\\\ning ServerlessLLM against a large-scale serverless workload,\\\\nmodelled on real-world serverless trace data.\\\\n7.1\\\\nEvaluation setup\\\\nSetup. In our study, we assess KServe and\\\\nServerlessLLM within a Kubernetes cluster. Given that our\\\\nfour-server cluster is unsuitable for a Kubernetes deployment,\\\\nwe instead utilize an eight-GPU server, simulating four nodes\\\\nwith two GPUs each. Since KServe performs slower than the\\\\nother baselines considered in our evaluation, we only briefly\\\\nmention KServe’s results without delving into details.\\\\nWith KServe, the GPU nodes initially exhibited a first to-\\\\nken latency of 128 seconds. This latency was primarily due to\\\\nKServe taking 114 seconds to download an OPT-6.7B model\\\\ncheckpoint from the local S3 storage over a 1 Gbps network.\\\\nHowever, after applying the same enhancement as those for\\\\nRay Serve, we reduced the first token latency to 28 seconds.\\\\nDespite this improvement, KServe’s best latency was signifi-\\\\ncantly higher than those achieved by ServerlessLLM. Notably,\\\\nServerlessLLM was the only system able to reduce the latency\\\\nto within one second.\\\\n8\\\\nRelated Work\\\\nServerless inference systems. Extensive research has aimed\\\\nto optimize ML model serving in serverless architectures,\\\\nfocusing on various aspects such as batching [3, 79, 84],\\\\nscheduling [58,82], and resource efficiency [20,40], among\\\\nothers [35]. Industry implementations include AWS Sage-\\\\nMaker and Azure ML [46], while KServe [11] represents an\\\\nopen-source initiative. Despite these advancements, current\\\\nserverless inference systems show suboptimal performance\\\\nwith LLMs, as evidenced by the experimental results shown in\\\\nthis paper. In this context, ServerlessLLM makes a significant\\\\ncontribution to serverless inference specifically for LLMs,\\\\naddressing their unique challenges of loading, migration, and\\\\nscheduling in a serverless environment.\\\\nServerless cold-start optimizations. Cold-start latency is a\\\\ncritical challenge in serverless systems. Numerous strategies\\\\nhave been devised to mitigate this issue, such as fast image\\\\npulling [75], lightweight isolation [42,50], snapshot and re-\\\\nstore [10,18,25,65,73], resource pre-provision [61], elastic\\\\nresource provisioning [45,74], and fork [2,76]. These solu-\\\\ntions primarily address the startup latency of containers or\\\\nVMs, which do not involve loading substantial external states.\\\\nWhile recent studies [36, 83] have sought to optimize cold-\\\\nstarts through accelerated model swapping between GPUs\\\\nand host memory, their scalability with LLMs remains limited.\\\\nIn contrast, ServerlessLLM effectively reduces the cold-start\\\\nlatency for LLMs by taking LLM-specific designs, includ-\\\\ning an LLM-optimized checkpoint format and its loading\\\\npipeline, LLM live migration and an LLM loading scheduler.\\\\nServerlessLLM’s approach is orthogonal to these optimiza-\\\\ntions specific to VMs and containers.\\\\nExploiting locality in serverless systems. Locality plays a\\\\ncrucial role in various optimization strategies for serverless\\\\nsystems. This includes leveraging host memory and local\\\\nstorage for data cache [38,57,67], optimizing the reading of\\\\nshared logs [37], and enhancing communication efficiency in\\\\nserverless Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) [43,44]. Server-\\\\nlessLLM, distinct from existing methods, introduces a high-\\\\nperformance checkpoint cache for GPUs, markedly improving\\\\ncheckpoint loading from multi-tier local storage to GPU mem-\\\\nory. Recent studies [1,81] have also recognized the need for\\\\nleveraging locality in orchestrating serverless functions. Be-\\\\nyond these studies, ServerlessLLM leverages LLM-specific\\\\ncharacteristics in improving the locality-based server’s selec-\\\\ntion and launching locality-driven inference.\\\\nLLM serving systems. LLM serving has recently seen signif-\\\\nicant strides, with numerous advancements optimizing infer-\\\\nence latency and throughput. Orca [80] introduces continuous\\\\nbatching to enhance GPU utilization during inference. Al-\\\\npaServe [41] demonstrates that model parallelism can boost\\\\nthroughput while adhering to SLO constraints. vLLM [39]\\\\ninnovates with PagedAttention for efficient KV cache man-\\\\nagement during LLM inference. SplitWise [53] capitalizes on\\\\nthe unique aspects of prompt and token generation in LLM\\\\ninference by distributing these phases across separate ma-\\\\nchines, effectively enhancing throughput. Additionally, some\\\\nsystems [8,63] explore leveraging storage devices to offload\\\\nparameters from GPUs when dealing with the substantial\\\\nsizes of state-of-the-art LLMs. However, these systems often\\\\nneglect the model loading challenge, resulting in extended\\\\nfirst token latencies when multiple models share GPUs for\\\\ninference. ServerlessLLM’s focus on minimizing loading la-\\\\ntency complements existing inference time optimizations.\\\\n9\\\\nConclusions\\\\nThis paper describes ServerlessLLM, a serverless inference\\\\nsystem purposefully designed for LLMs. The design of\\\\nServerlessLLM uncovers significant opportunities for sys-\\\\ntem research, including designing new loading-optimized\\\\ncheckpoints, discovering the need to support live migration\\\\nwhen conducting locality-driven LLM inference, and en-\\\\nabling latency-preserving, locality-driven server allocation\\\\nin a serverless cluster. We believe our work can be extended\\\\nto ensure fairness of resources across the entire cluster and\\\\nexplore the possibility of smart checkpoint placement. We\\\\nlook forward to addressing these issues in the future. We con-\\\\nsider ServerlessLLM as the first step towards unlocking the\\\\npotential of serverless computing for LLMs and reducing the\\\\ntime to inference. We plan to open-source ServerlessLLM.\\\\nGiven its versatility, we envision it as a platform to test new\\\\nresearch ideas.\\\\n13\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 14 ===\\\\nReferences\\\\n[1] Mania Abdi, Samuel Ginzburg, Xiayue Charles Lin,\\\\nJose Faleiro, Gohar Irfan Chaudhry, Inigo Goiri, Ri-\\\\ncardo Bianchini, Daniel S Berger, and Rodrigo Fon-\\\\nseca. It supports\\\\nhigh-availability applications with runtime features that min-\\\\nimize fault-recovery time, and scheduling policies that re-\\\\nduce the probability of correlated failures. Borg simpliﬁes\\\\nlife for its users by offering a declarative job speciﬁcation\\\\nlanguage, name service integration, real-time job monitor-\\\\ning, and tools to analyze and simulate system behavior.\\\\nWe present a summary of the Borg system architecture\\\\nand features, important design decisions, a quantitative anal-\\\\nysis of some of its policy decisions, and a qualitative ex-\\\\namination of lessons learned from a decade of operational\\\\nexperience with it.\\\\n1.\\\\nIntroduction\\\\nThe cluster management system we internally call Borg ad-\\\\nmits, schedules, starts, restarts, and monitors the full range\\\\nof applications that Google runs. This paper explains how.\\\\nBorg provides three main beneﬁts: it (1) hides the details\\\\nof resource management and failure handling so its users can\\\\nfocus on application development instead; (2) operates with\\\\nvery high reliability and availability, and supports applica-\\\\ntions that do the same; and (3) lets us run workloads across\\\\ntens of thousands of machines effectively. Borg is not the\\\\nﬁrst system to address these issues, but it’s one of the few op-\\\\nerating at this scale, with this degree of resiliency and com-\\\\npleteness.
